Enhancements: - Refine CMS posts table layout, including column widths and date display logic that prefers scheduled or published dates when available. - Introduce an improved empty-state experience for the posts table with guidance and a direct action to create the first post. - Refactor the posts index page content into a dedicated component to simplify structure and make it easier to reuse or extend. - Simplify post creation cache invalidation by evicting the posts list field without relying on mutation result data. ---- > [!IMPORTANT] > Enhance CMS post management with improved cache handling, UI adjustments, and refined post submission logic. > > - **Cache Management**: > - Updated `usePostMutations` in `usePostMutations.ts` to evict cache for `cmsPostList` after post creation and editing. > - Added cache eviction logic for individual post edits in `usePostMutations.ts`. > - **UI Adjustments**: > - Commented out status change logic in `PostMoreColumn.tsx`. > - Adjusted column sizes in `PostsColumn.tsx`. > - Added empty state UI in `PostsRecordTable.tsx` when no posts are available. > - **Post Submission Logic**: > - Updated `usePostSubmission.tsx` to handle empty descriptions and generate slugs for new posts. > - Added `publishDate` field handling in `AddPostHeaderActions.tsx`. > - **Miscellaneous**: > - Refactored `PostsPage.tsx` to separate content rendering logic. > > This description was created by [](https://www.ellipsis.dev?ref=erxes%2Ferxes&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral) for 2b93c186a870e9dc8e8f364be6522eec9fdfe18d. author: copilot
body:
`MultiSearchWithMetadata` was missing `vald.MetadataSpanName` in its span name and gRPC method string, causing traces for this RPC to appear as a non-metadata call — inconsistent with every other `*WithMetadata` RPC in the file.

## Change

- Append `+vald.MetadataSpanName` to both `grpc.WithGRPCMethod(...)` and the span name in `MultiSearchWithMetadata`:

```go
// Before
ctx, span := trace.StartSpan(
    grpc.WithGRPCMethod(ctx, vald.PackageName+"."+vald.SearchRPCServiceName+"/"+vald.MultiSearchRPCName),
    apiName+"/"+vald.MultiSearchRPCName,
)

// After
ctx, span := trace.StartSpan(
    grpc.WithGRPCMethod(ctx, vald.PackageName+"."+vald.SearchRPCServiceName+"/"+vald.MultiSearchRPCName+vald.MetadataSpanName),
    apiName+"/"+vald.MultiSearchRPCName+vald.MetadataSpanName,
)
```

This aligns `MultiSearchWithMetadata` with `MultiSearchByIDWithMetadata`, `MultiLinearSearchWithMetadata`, and all other `*WithMetadata` handlers.

author: suzyeaston
body:
### Motivation
- The bio opening-crawl began off-screen and theme styles were overriding the intended large yellow crawl, so the crawl needs to start with the title visible and present a consistent large yellow opening-crawl look while still respecting reduced-motion.

### Description
- Start the crawl nearer the visible area by setting `.bio-crawl { bottom: 6%; transform: ... translateY(20%); }` and update `@keyframes bioCrawl` to animate from `translateY(20%)` to `translateY(-220%)` so the title/subtitle appear immediately and the crawl travels upward smoothly.
- Increase and normalize typography by adding `font-size: clamp(18px, 1.6vw, 24px)`, `line-height: 1.75`, `font-weight: 700`, and larger title/subtitle clamps (`.bio-crawl-title` and `.bio-crawl-subtitle`).
- Force the crawl color to the warm yellow with `.bio-crawl, .bio-crawl * { color: #f5d24a !important; }` and keep links readable with underline and a hover/focus color shift so theme colors do not bleed in.
- Add a non-interactive vignette overlay on the crawl container via `.bio-crawl-wrap::before` for a subtle top fade and hide that overlay in `prefers-reduced-motion`, and preserve reduced-motion by disabling the animation and tilt and falling back to a static readable layout.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check` which returned clean results for the edited CSS.
- Executed a Playwright-based screenshot attempt against local `/bio/` endpoints, but the navigation failed with `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` so visual verification could not be captured in this environment.

author: jheikkila42
body:
### Motivation

- Extend scheduling to support special operations (sluice and shifting) and enforce related staffing rules during port ops.
- Provide a more robust Streamlit UI with manual Day 1 editing and post-generation inline editing to allow quick adjustments and re-generate Excel output.
- Improve STCW analysis helpers and add test organization and a small CLI to run test groups.

### Description

- Rewrote `app.py` to a more feature-rich Streamlit frontend that adds manual Day 1 editing (`data_editor`), post-generation editor, session-state storage of generated results, improved time parsing, half-day table views, and Excel rebuild compatibility via `build_workbook_and_report`/`generate_schedule_with_manual_day1` integration.  Key helpers: `ensure_sea_watch_time_helpers`, `convert_manual_df_to_slots`, `create_editable_work_df`, and `render_post_generation_editor`.
- Enhanced `sea_watch_10.py` with support for `sluice` and `shifting` operations, new coloring/Excel labels, stricter/outside-worker rules (single worker during outside-op slots), trimming of redundant short segments, departure locking, and helper APIs: `analyze_stcw_from_work_starts`, `_trim_redundant_short_segments`, `_enforce_single_outside_op_worker`, `build_workbook_and_report`, and `generate_schedule_with_manual_day1`.
- Added test organization and a CLI: `pytest.ini` defines markers for focused groups, and `run_tests.py` provides `python run_tests.py <group>` (e.g. `all`, `special-ops`).
- Updated tests and utilities in `test_sea_watch.py` and `test_print_excel` to cover the new sluice/shifting behavior, STCW marker-based tests, daily hour checks and short-segment cleanup.
- Minor README additions demonstrating how to run grouped tests and listing the STCW checks used by the analyzer.

### Testing

- Ran the full test suite with the provided runner using `python run_tests.py all` (internally runs `pytest -q`) and observed all tests passing for the modified test files.
- Executed focused groups during development such as `python run_tests.py special-ops` and `python run_tests.py stcw-rest` to validate new sluice/shifting and STCW checks, and they succeeded.

body:
### Motivation
- Align Netty injector behavior with the ProtocolLib bridge by parsing client movement packets into `MovementFrame` instances and dispatching them through the same movement pipeline. 
- Centralize movement frame consumption so Bukkit `PlayerMoveEvent` and packet-dispatched frames use the same logic to avoid source-driven branch drift. 
- Fail gracefully when reflection-based packet field extraction cannot resolve values and fall back to the existing internal-event-only path while emitting a configurable warning. 

### Description
- Added movement packet recognition and parsing in `PacketPipelineInjector`: introduced `isMovementPacket(...)`, `tryDispatchMovementFrame(...)`, `toMovementSource(...)` and a `LocationSnapshot` fallback; parsed `PacketPlayInFlying/Position/Look/PositionLook` into `MovementFrame` with correct `hasPosition`/`hasLook` and `Source`, then call `plugin.movementFrames().dispatch(player, frame)`. 
- Added reflection helpers to `PacketPipelineInjector` for multi-name double reads and typed reads: overloaded `readDoubleField(...preferredNames)`, `readFloatField(...)`, and `readBooleanField(...)`. 
- When parsing fails, call `warnReflectionFailureOnce(..., "movement-frame")` respecting `netty.strict-reflection` and return without interrupting packet flow or internal movement event emission. 
- Refactored `CheckManager` to introduce `consumeMovementFrame(...)` and have both `onMove(...)` and `onMovementFrame(...)` delegate to it so both Bukkit and packet sources follow the same execution path.

body:
## Overview

When our API calls fail, we weren't properly validating the response before trying to parse JSON. This meant applications would throw unhandled promise rejections instead of handling errors gracefully.

## Changes

Added response.ok checks in two critical API functions:

- **getTaxo()**: Now validates the response before parsing taxonomy data from our taxonomy API
- **getFacetKnowledgePanels()**: Now validates the response before parsing facet knowledge panel data

When an API returns an error status, we now throw a descriptive error message with the response status text. This gives us better visibility into what went wrong and prevents silent failures.

## Why It Matters

Without these checks, failed API responses would lead to:
- Unhandled promise rejections in the JavaScript console
- Confusing error states in the UI
- Difficult debugging when third-party APIs have issues

Now we handle these failures explicitly at the source, making error handling predictable across the application.

## Testing

Both functions are now wrapped with proper error handling. The application should handle API errors gracefully without console warnings about unhandled rejections.

Resolves #986

author: toddwbucy
body:
## Summary

Fixes a pre-existing gap where `batch_size > 1` resume always restarted from partition-start offsets rather than the actual mid-slot positions where training stopped.

**Root cause**: the step loop consumes `bpe_loaders[b]` (per-slot), but checkpoint saves wrote `active_loader.cursor()` — which is never advanced in multi-slot mode (position always 0). On resume, `bpe_loaders` was reconstructed from scratch ignoring the sidecar entirely.

**Fix**:
- **Save**: when `bpe_loaders` is non-empty, write `{"slots": [loader.cursor() for loader in bpe_loaders]}`. Single-slot path (`active_loader.cursor()`) is unchanged.
- **Resume**: after constructing `bpe_loaders`, if a sidecar exists with a matching-length `"slots"` list, restore each `loader_b` from its saved cursor. Slot-count mismatch (e.g. batch_size changed between runs) prints a warning and falls back to partition-start — does not abort.

**Sidecar schema** (backwards-compatible):
```
single-slot (batch_size=1):  {position, total_tokens, content_hash, ...}
multi-slot  (batch_size > 1): {"slots": [{...}, {...}, ...]}
```

## Test plan

- [x] `test_multi_slot_cursor_roundtrip` — save+restore per-slot positions, assert each position/chunk_id matches
- [x] `test_single_slot_sidecar_unchanged` — batch_size=1 sidecar is still a flat cursor dict (no `slots` wrapper)
- [x] `test_slot_count_mismatch_resets` — 3-slot sidecar + 2-slot bpe_loaders falls back to partition-start, no abort
- [x] All 44 Python tests pass (41 pre-existing + 3 new)

author: codier
body:
## Problem

When a token is not tracked by Nansen's price oracle, `nansen research token ohlcv` returns `null` for all price fields (`open`, `high`, `low`, `close`, `volume_usd`, `market_cap`) while `volume` is still populated (volume comes from on-chain DEX data and is always available).

Previously this was **silent** — the response looked valid but was half-empty, misleading for both humans and AI agents consuming the output.

**Reproduced with:**
```
nansen research token ohlcv \
  --token 0x4ed4E862860beD51a9570b96d89aF5E1B0Efefed \
  --chain base --timeframe 1d
```

## Fix

Added a post-response check in the `token` command handler that detects this condition and emits a clear warning to stderr:

```
⚠️  Price data unavailable for this token on base.
   open/high/low/close, volume_usd, and market_cap are null.
   Volume (raw token units) is available. This token may not be tracked by Nansen's price oracle.
```

The warning is emitted to **stderr** so it doesn't pollute JSON output when piping. The data is still returned as-is so downstream consumers can decide what to do with it.

## Behaviour

| Condition | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Price null, volume present | ⚠️ warning to stderr |
| Price null, volume also null | ⚠️ generic "no data" warning |
| Full price data | No warning (clean output) |

## Tests

2 new unit tests in `cli.internal.test.js`:
- ✅ Null price + volume present → warning emitted
- ✅ Full price data → no warning

All 704 tests pass.

No mechanism existed for nodes to discover each other on the LAN or exchange pending jobs, making cross-peer job draining impossible.

## Changes

### `configs/configs.py`
- Added `enable_lan_peer_discovery` (bool, default `False`), `lan_peer_port` (int, default `8765`), `lan_discovery_port` (int, default `8766`)

### `external_interface/peer_discovery/peer_discovery.py` *(new)*
- `PeerDiscovery`: UDP broadcast-based peer registry with 10 s announce interval, 60 s TTL eviction, and **source IP validation** – announcements from non-RFC-1918 addresses are discarded before any state mutation

### `external_interface/peer_job_drainer/peer_job_drainer.py` *(new)*
- `PeerJobServer`: aiohttp server exposing `GET /jobs` and `POST /jobs/claim`; the claim endpoint atomically removes job IDs from the local queue
- `PeerJobDrainer`: HTTP client that fetches and claims all available jobs from a peer, placing them into the local `asyncio.Queue`; `drain_from_all_peers()` runs concurrently across the full peer set

```python
# Drain jobs from all discovered peers when local queue is empty
peers = discovery.get_peers()          # {("192.168.1.x", 8765), ...}
drained = await drainer.drain_from_all_peers(peers)
```

### Tests
- 18 unit/integration tests covering announcement parsing, peer eviction, private-IP validation, HTTP server endpoints, single-peer and multi-peer draining, and error paths (unreachable peer, empty queue, malformed claim body)

{

body:
### Motivation
- Fix the bug where messages that `@mention` the active user highlight correctly but do not reliably cause the chat to scroll to the bottom. 
- Preserve user reading flow by using a Twitch-like strategy that avoids forcing scrolls when the user is browsing history. 
- Ensure mobile/browser stability by scheduling scrolls after DOM/layout updates and provide debug controls to validate behavior.

### Description
- Implemented mention autoscroll logic in `src/ui/chat/ChatPanel.tsx` that inspects new incoming messages and, for `new message + non-self + message.mentions` hitting `activeUser`, will either auto-scroll when near-bottom or pulse a jump hint when the user is reading older messages. 
- Added robust scroll scheduling (`requestAnimationFrame` + `setTimeout(0)`) and a `MENTION_AUTOSCROLL_THRESHOLD` (100px) to avoid missed scrolls on mobile/Android browsers. 
- Added UI/debug features: a pulsing `@你・跳到最新` jump button state, URL flag `forceMentionAutoscroll=1`, and a debug button `Inject NPC Tag @You` (wired in `src/app/App.tsx`), plus styles in `src/styles.css`. 
- Updated documentation: `README.md`, `docs/10-change-log.md`, and `PR_NOTES.md` to describe the behavior, strategy rationale (Strategy B), acceptance tests and debug instructions.

### Testing
- Ran static/type build: `npx tsc -b` completed successfully. 
- Attempted production build with `npm run build` but the container environment failed due to a missing optional native rollup package (`@rollup/rollup-linux-x64-gnu`), so full `vite build` could not complete in this environment. 
- Ran dev server with `npm run dev` and validated UI startup; captured a Playwright screenshot of the running app at `browser:/tmp/codex_browser_invocations/36332dc4d947951f/artifacts/artifacts/mention-autoscroll.png`. 
- Manual / functional verification steps are documented in `PR_NOTES.md` (include cases: at-bottom autoscroll, non-bottom jump hint, and burst messages stability).

author: ivankatliarchuk
body:
## What does it do ?

EndpointsForHostname lives in source/endpoints.go (package source) but belongs conceptually in the endpoint package — it only deals with endpoint.* types and logic.

related: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/external-dns/pull/6239

## Motivation

  1. Correct package placement
  EndpointsForHostname only operates on endpoint.* types (Targets, TTL, ProviderSpecific, Endpoint). Having it live in the source package was a layering violation — source imports endpoint, not the other way around. Moving it down to endpoint puts it where it semantically belongs.

  2. Broader reusability without importing source
  Before, any package needing this function had to import the entire source package (which pulls in Kubernetes informers, controllers, etc.). source/wrappers/multisource.go was already doing this awkwardly. Now anything that imports endpoint (a lightweight, foundational package) gets the function for free.

  3. Eliminated repetitive code
  The original had three near-identical blocks (~55 lines) for A, AAAA, and CNAME — copy-paste with only the record type and target slice varying. The refactored version is  ~20 lines with a single loop.

author: sushil-19
body:
This PR reduces allocations in `mapRenderer.writeFinishedMaps` by preallocating
`mapIndices` and `rows` with a bounded capacity.

Previously, both slices were declared without capacity hints:

```
var mapIndices []uint32
var rows []FilterRow
```

This caused repeated slice growth and reallocations inside a hot loop during
log index rendering.

The updated implementation computes a bounded capacity per row:

```
base := len(r.finishedMaps)
extra := 0
if newRange.maps.AfterLast() == r.finished.AfterLast() {
    if oldRange.maps.AfterLast() > r.finished.AfterLast() {
        extra = int(oldRange.maps.AfterLast() - r.finished.AfterLast())
    }
}
capacity := base + extra

mapIndices := make([]uint32, 0, capacity)
rows := make([]FilterRow, 0, capacity)
```

Since `r.finishedMaps` is bounded (<= maxMapsPerBatch, currently 32), and
`extra` is only added when ranges overlap (with an explicit guard against
underflow), the resulting capacity remains safely bounded.

This avoids repeated slice growth and reallocation in a hot path during
log index rendering.

Validation:

* `go test ./core/filtermaps` passes
* Full test suite passes
* Benchmarks (`go test -bench . -benchmem`) pass
* Memory profiling confirms reduced allocation pressure in this path

No functional changes.

body:
## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature  
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation update

## Motivation and Context

Closes #1252 (part of #913).

Commands that accept `--platform` currently require it to be passed explicitly every time. Users working consistently with a non-native platform (e.g. `linux/amd64` on Apple Silicon) have no way to set a default, unlike Docker's `DOCKER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM`.

This adds support for the `CONTAINER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM` environment variable as a fallback when `--platform` is not explicitly provided.

## Changes

- **New file `DefaultPlatform.swift`** — centralized logic for reading, validating, and resolving the environment variable with clear precedence rules.
- **Wired into all commands with `--platform`:** `run`, `create`, `image pull`, `image push`, `image save`, and `build`.
- **Precedence:** explicit `--platform` flag → `--os`/`--arch` flags → `CONTAINER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM` → native host architecture.
- **User feedback:** prints a notice to stderr when the environment variable is active (e.g. `Notice: Using platform "linux/amd64" from CONTAINER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM`).
- **Help text:** all `--platform` options now show `[environment: CONTAINER_DEFAULT_PLATFORM]`.
- **Error handling:** invalid values in the environment variable produce a clear error message naming the variable.

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added/updated tests
- [ ] Added/updated docs

20 unit tests added in `DefaultPlatformTests.swift` covering:
- Environment variable parsing (valid platforms, empty, missing, invalid)
- Precedence for `resolve()` (pull/push/save): explicit flags override env var
- Precedence for `resolveWithDefaults()` (run/create): env var overrides os/arch defaults
- Invalid env var is skipped when explicit `--platform` is provided
- All 134 pre-existing unit tests pass with no regressions

author: yaskhan
body:
Fixes scoping issues with variables assigned in if/else blocks

Python's `if/else` does not create a new variable scope, but Vlang does. Consequently, variables initialized only within a V block are inaccessible outside. If a variable is assigned conditionally for the first time, it causes transpiled V code to fail compilation.

This patch improves variable scoping generation by tracking local declarations per function/method. The transpiler now analyzes `if` and `else` blocks, collects newly assigned variables (including destructuring assignments while ignoring loop targets), and safely pre-declares them before the conditional block as `mut msg := ?Type(none)`. Subsequent assignments inside the block correctly use `=` instead of `:=`. The corresponding task in `todo2.md` has been marked as completed.

author: murphisensei
body:
## Summary

- **Problem**: `<file>` blocks in user messages (from PDF/Excel/Word attachments processed by the media pipeline) can be 200K+ chars but are never pruned by `contextPruning`, causing system prompt rules (e.g. SOUL.md output hygiene) to be pushed out of the model's effective attention window
- **Solution**: Add a new `fileBlocks` config section under `contextPruning` that trims oversized `<file>` blocks in user messages to head+tail summaries, running before the existing tool result trimming pass
- **Config**: `contextPruning.fileBlocks.{enabled, maxChars, headChars, tailChars}` with sensible defaults (enabled=true, 2000/800/800)
- **Backward compatible**: enabled by default, opt-out via `fileBlocks.enabled: false`

## Changes

- `settings.ts`: Add `fileBlocks` type definition, defaults, and config parsing
- `types.agent-defaults.ts`: Add `fileBlocks` optional field to `AgentContextPruningConfig`
- `zod-schema.agent-defaults.ts`: Add `fileBlocks` validation schema
- `pruner.ts`: Add `softTrimFileBlocksInText()` and `softTrimFileBlocksInUserMessage()` functions; integrate file block trimming pass into `pruneContextMessages()` before existing tool result trimming
- `context-pruning.test.ts`: Add 8 test cases covering unit trimming, string/array content, multi-block, integration with tool result trimming, enabled=false, and keepLastAssistants protection

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm tsgo` — zero type errors
- [x] `pnpm check` — lint + format pass
- [x] `pnpm test -- --run context-pruning.test.ts` — all 19 tests pass (10 existing + 8 new file block tests + 1 settings test)

author: lyokone
body:
## Description

Fix native crash on Windows when using `DocumentReference` as a query filter or field value.

The codec's `DATA_TYPE_FIRESTORE_INSTANCE` handler used `appName` as cache key, while `GetFirestoreFromPigeon` uses `appName + "-" + databaseUrl`. This caused a cache miss, creating a second `unique_ptr` wrapping the same `Firestore*` — double-free on teardown.

Fixed by using the same composite key and passing `databaseUrl` to `Firestore::GetInstance`.

## Summary

author: vishnub-atlan
body:
## Summary

- Adds a `compression` parameter to `ParquetFileWriter` (default: `"snappy"`, supports `snappy`, `zstd`, `gzip`, `none`) so callers can choose the parquet compression codec at construction time.
- Forces Daft's PyArrow-based writer (`native_parquet_writer=False`) because the native Rust writer silently ignores the `compression` kwarg and hardcodes SNAPPY.
- Derives row counts from written parquet file metadata (`pyarrow.parquet.read_metadata`) instead of calling `dataframe.count_rows()`, avoiding a full re-materialisation of lazy Daft DataFrames.
- Replaces `count_rows()` emptiness checks with `limit(1).count_rows() == 0` to prevent materialising the entire DataFrame just to check if it's empty.
- Threads the chosen compression through `estimate_dataframe_record_size`, the pandas write path (`to_parquet`), and the Daft consolidation write path.

## Changed files

| File | What changed |
|------|-------------|
| `application_sdk/io/parquet.py` | New `compression` param, validation, `native_parquet_writer=False`, metadata-based row counting |
| `application_sdk/io/__init__.py` | Pass `compression` to `estimate_dataframe_record_size` |
| `application_sdk/io/utils.py` | Accept `compression` param in `estimate_dataframe_record_size`; use `limit(1)` in `is_empty_dataframe` |
| `tests/unit/io/writers/test_parquet_writer.py` | New test classes for compression config, codec verification (real writes), and `estimate_dataframe_record_size` passthrough; updated existing daft tests for new mocks |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for compression parameter validation (default, valid, invalid)
- [x] Unit tests verifying compression is threaded to pandas, daft, and consolidation write paths
- [x] Integration-style tests that perform real parquet writes and assert the codec in file metadata (zstd, snappy)
- [x] Existing daft writer tests updated with `read_metadata` / `get_object_store_prefix` mocks
- [ ] CI passes all pre-existing and new tests

author: donalotiarnaigh
body:
## Summary

- `validateAndConvertTypes()` in `src/utils/dataValidation.js` previously used `logger.warn()` (suppressible by `quietMode`) on JSON parse failure, silently returned `null` for the failed field, and left `needs_review` unchanged — corrupted records passed through undetected.
- `confidence_scores` and `validation_warnings` were missing from the JSON-parse field list entirely, so they were never parsed on retrieval.
- Fix extends the field list, switches to `logger.error()` (always calls `console.error()` regardless of sampling/quietMode), and forces `needs_review = 1` on any record with a parse failure.

## Changes

author: jasonoa888
body:
## Summary

Implements #13132: Short-circuit `--version`/`-V` before loading modules (~100x faster).

## Problem

`openclaw --version` takes ~5 seconds on constrained environments because it loads all modules before parsing the flag.

## Solution

Add early exit in bootstrap (`openclaw.mjs`) with proper root invocation detection:
- `isRootVersionInvocation()` detects root vs subcommand
- Only triggers for root commands (`openclaw --version`)
- Skips for subcommands (`openclaw status --version`)
- Uses `-V` (uppercase) to avoid conflict with `-v` (`--verbose`)

## Performance

| Environment | Before | After |
|-------------|--------|-------|
| Constrained VPS | ~5s | **<50ms** |

**100x faster!**

## Testing

```bash
time node openclaw.mjs --version
# 2026.3.3
# real 0m0.048s ✅

time node openclaw.mjs -V
# 2026.3.3
# real 0m0.045s ✅
```

Fixes #13132

🦞

### Motivation

- Provide an automated CI job to build the 360 AP1PA3 firmware to simplify producing and collecting firmware artifacts.
- Ensure repository uses the pinned `buildroot` submodule state rather than updating to the remote tip during builds.
- Enable Ethernet and the USB-R8152 driver in the device defconfig so built images include required network support.

### Description

- Add a new workflow `build-360_ap1pa3.yml` that checks out the repo, installs build dependencies, runs `BOARD=360_ap1pa3_t31x_gc4653_atbm6031 make fast`, and uploads firmware artifacts.
- Configure workflow triggers for `push` on main/master/stable and `workflow_dispatch` with an optional `branch` input, and add concurrency to cancel in-progress runs for the same ref.
- Change `Makefile` submodule handling to initialize and update the `buildroot` submodule with `git submodule update --init --recursive` and correct the comment to reflect pinning.
- Update `configs/cameras/360_ap1pa3_t31x_gc4653_atbm6031_defconfig` to enable `BR2_ETHERNET` and `BR2_PACKAGE_USBNET_R8152` so the kernel/image includes Ethernet and the R8152 USB network driver.

author: shubho0908
body:
<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary of Changes

This PR refactors the API to adopt a service-first architecture, removing intermediate controller wrappers, consolidating scattered utilities, and reorganizing modules for clarity. The changes establish cleaner separation of concerns and simplify the request flow from routes directly to use-cases/services.

### 🔴 Security-Sensitive Changes
**None identified.** No authentication, authorization, or credential handling was weakened. Environment variable setup and configuration routing remain intact.

---

## Major Refactoring Patterns

### 1. **Removal of Pass-Through Controller Wrappers**
- Deleted controller files and functions that merely delegated to internal services:
  - `controllers/apiKey.controller.ts` → import directly from `services/apiKey/apiKey.useCase.ts`
  - `controllers/chat/message.controller.ts` → use `services/runs/messageOrchestrator.service.ts`
  - `controllers/chat/session/session.controller.ts` → use `services/chat/session/orchestrator/`
  - `controllers/chat/subdomain.controller.ts` → use `services/previewRouting/subdomainUpdate.service.ts`
  - `controllers/github.controller.ts` → import from `services/github/github.useCase.ts`
  - Similar removals for query controllers (build, history, run, sandbox)

**Impact:** Routes now import directly from services/use-cases, reducing indirection and simplifying the call chain.

### 2. **Reorganization of Agent Loop and Session Logic**
- **Moved** agent loop from `controllers/chat/session/loop/internal/agentLoop.runner.ts` → `services/chat/session/loop/agentLoop.runner.ts`
- **Removed** wrapper exports in `controllers/chat/session/loop/agent.loop.ts`
- **Refactored** stream session orchestration utilities into focused modules:
  - `runStreamSession.orchestrator.ts`, `runStreamSession.content.ts`, `runStreamSession.finalize.ts`, etc.
- **Added** new supporting modules: `agentLoop.stream.ts`, `agentLoop.turnOutcome.ts`, `processor.events.ts`, `processor.finalize.ts`, `processor.session.ts`, `processor.ts`

**Impact:** Core streaming and agent logic now lives in services with clearer separation of concerns (stream handling, turn outcomes, finalization).

### 3. **Consolidation of Query Operations**
- **Created** dedicated use-case modules:
  - `services/chat/query/build.useCase.ts` – build status streaming
  - `services/chat/query/history.useCase.ts` & `history.repository.ts` – chat history and metadata
  - `services/chat/query/run.useCase.ts` & `run.repository.ts` – run status and cancellation
  - `services/chat/query/sandbox.useCase.ts` – sandbox file access
  - `services/chat/query/requestContext.ts` – context helpers
  - `services/chat/query/query.useCaseError.ts` – error handling
- **Centralized** error response via `sendQueryErrorResponse.ts` in controllers

**Impact:** Query logic is now testable, reusable, and follows a consistent pattern with explicit error boundaries.

### 4. **Module Flattening and Path Simplification**
- **Removed** nested re-export modules (`steps.ts`, `spaFallback.ts`, `backupReader.ts`, `snapshotReader.ts`, etc.)
- **Updated** import paths to point directly to implementation modules (e.g., `services/planning/workflow/steps/executeAnalyzePhase.ts` instead of a wrapper)
- **Consolidated** SSE utilities from `controllers/chat/sse.utils.ts` → `services/sse-utils/service.js`
- **Moved** parser content/shared logic into `lib/llm/parser.*.ts` modules with clear separation

**Impact:** Fewer indirection layers, more predictable module structure, easier to trace dependencies.

### 5. **Extraction of Worker Handlers**
- **Created** `services/queue/workerJobHandlers.service.ts` with:
  - `processBuildJob()` – orchestrates build lifecycle with status publishing
  - `processBackupJob()` – handles backup operations
  - `processAgentRun()` – delegates to agent run processor
- **Added** `services/queue/workerPolicies.ts` with retry, timeout, and status helpers
- **Removed** the large monolithic processor from `services/runs/agentRun.worker/processor.ts`; logic split into focused helpers

**Impact:** Worker jobs now have explicit, testable handlers with clear timeout/retry policies. Easier to debug and monitor.

### 6. **Restructuring of Sandbox and Storage Services**
- **Removed** wrapper modules (`read.service.ts` for S3, `backupReader.ts`, `legacyReader.ts`, etc.)
- **Created** lifecycle management: `services/sandbox/lifecycle/runtimeLifecycle.store.ts` (state machine for sandbox provisioning/cleanup)
- **Consolidated** build orchestration: unified-build paths, SPA fallback runtime scripts split into dedicated modules
- **Added** command output utilities: `services/tools/commandOutput.ts` for sanitization/deduplication

**Impact:** Sandbox state transitions are now tracked explicitly; build output handling is isolated and testable.

### 7. **Removal of Diagnostic Services**
- **Deleted** entire diagnostic subsystem: `services/diagnostics/` directory including:
  - Parser modules for TypeScript, Next.js, Vite, generic error parsing
  - Schema categorization and error extraction
  - Public functions like `extractDiagnostics()`, `suggestAction()`, etc.

**Impact:** Diagnostic extraction moved elsewhere or deprecated; verify if needed for error reporting in the new architecture.

### 8. **Type and Export Consolidation**
- **Removed** re-exports from schemas (e.g., `ParserEventType` now imports from `@edward/shared/streamEvents`)
- **Moved** token usage types to `lib/llm/tokens/usage.types.ts`
- **Updated** checkpoint types to `services/chat/session/shared/checkpoint.types.ts`
- **Removed** public type wrappers in various service modules

**Impact:** Single source of truth for types; clearer dependencies; reduced circular imports.

---

## New Public APIs and Test Coverage

### Added Use-Case & Repository Patterns
- **Chat query use-cases**: `getBuildStatusUseCase()`, `getChatHistoryUseCase()`, `deleteChatUseCase()`, `getActiveRunUseCase()`, `cancelRunUseCase()`, `getSandboxFilesUseCase()`, etc.
- **Repository helpers**: `getLatestBuildRecord()`, `getMessagesByChatId()`, `getActiveRunRecord()`, `cancelActiveRun()`, etc.
- **Worker handlers**: `processBuildJob()`, `processBackupJob()`, `processAgentRun()`
- **Middleware & utilities**: `createHttpApp()` factory, new rate limit and security telemetry tests

### Updated Tests
- **Deleted** controller-level delegation tests (no longer needed)
- **Added** comprehensive unit tests for:
  - New use-case modules (build, history, run, sandbox queries)
  - Worker job handlers and shutdown behavior
  - Queue routing and job dispatch
  - Route registration and schema contracts
  - Middleware (rate limiting, security)
  - Sandbox lifecycle state machine
- **Migrated** test imports from `controllers/` to `services/` paths

---

## Key Risks & Mitigation

### ⚠️ **Risk: Incomplete Migration of Diagnostic Logic**
- Diagnostic extraction, categorization, and error reporting were removed wholesale
- No clear indication where this functionality migrated to
- **Mitigation**: Verify that error reporting (build failures, compilation errors) still surfaces to users via build status events and error messages

### ⚠️ **Risk: Changed Worker Behavior**
- Worker processor rewritten from monolithic to modular
- New state tracking via `RunEventProgress`, `PersistedRunState` enums
- **Mitigation**: Extensive new tests added (`processor.events.ts`, `processor.finalize.ts`, `processor.helpers.ts`); verify integration tests cover end-to-end agent runs

### ⚠️ **Risk: Sandbox Lifecycle State Machine Introduced**
- New enum `SandboxLifecycleState` (PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, CLEANING_UP, TERMINATED, FAILED)
- State transitions in provisioning, cleanup, and monitoring
- **Mitigation**: State is Redis-backed with 24-hour expiry; test confirms transitions are atomic and handle missing states

### ⚠️ **Risk: Parser and LLM Token Handling Reorganized**
- Parser refactored to m

### Motivation
- The signup flows called `crypto.randomUUID()` directly, which throws `crypto.randomUUID is not a function` in runtimes (older browsers/webviews) where the API is unavailable.  
- Provide a secure, compatible fallback so account creation doesn't crash on unsupported clients.

### Description
- Add a helper `generateUserId()` in `phishing_shield/PWA_frontend/src/app/lib/auth.ts` that uses `crypto.randomUUID()` when present.  
- Implement a standards-compliant UUID v4 fallback that uses `crypto.getRandomValues()` to generate a UUID string.  
- Replace direct `crypto.randomUUID()` calls in `signupWithPassword` and `completeGoogleSignup` with `generateUserId()`.

author: shubham-sumo
body:
bump golang and its dependencies to newer versions


After upgrading dependencies test started with the following error 

```
Failure [0.000 seconds]
handler
/home/runner/work/tailing-sidecar/tailing-sidecar/operator/handler/handler_test.go:53
  PodExtender.Handle
  /home/runner/work/tailing-sidecar/tailing-sidecar/operator/handler/handler_test.go:146
    when Pod with existing tailing sidecar
    /home/runner/work/tailing-sidecar/tailing-sidecar/operator/handler/handler_test.go:768
      returns patch without tailing sidecar containers [It]
      /home/runner/work/tailing-sidecar/tailing-sidecar/operator/handler/handler_test.go:877

      Expected
          <[]jsonpatch.Operation | len:1, cap:1>: [
              {
                  Operation: "remove",
                  Path: "/metadata/creationTimestamp",
                  Value: nil,
              },
          ]
      to be empty
      
  ```
  
  Upon investigation it was found that `omitzero` was recently added to `CreationTimestamp` field in https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/v0.35.2/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go#L188
  
 The `omitzero` tag causes the encoder to omit zero-valued fields entirely, rather than encoding them as null. This creates a mismatch when comparing the original API request JSON (which has explicit null) with the re-marshaled JSON (which omits the field).




This PR changes the test cases to make creationTimeStamp non null

body:
## やったこと

- tsdown の version up

## 動作確認環境
- CI

## チェックリスト
- build が通ること

不要なチェック項目は消して構いません

- [X] 破壊的変更がある場合には、対象のパッケージのメジャーバージョンが上がっていることを確認した
- [X] 追加したコンポーネントが index.ts から再 export されている
- [X] README やドキュメントに影響があることを確認した

## 備考 tsdown 0.15 → 0.20.x 変更まとめ

### v0.16.0
Release: https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/releases/tag/v0.16.0

#### Breaking Changes

- Config 型名のリネーム (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/519, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/7de20b2)
  - Options → UserConfig / InlineConfig
  - NormalizedUserConfig → UserConfig
  - ResolvedOptions → ResolvedConfig
- fixedExtension が platform: 'node' でデフォルト true に (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/517, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/e1168a2)
  - .js が .mjs / .cjs に変わる。package.json の type に依存しなくなる
  - main, module, types, exports, bin フィールドに影響
- --debug CLI フラグ → --debug-logs (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/576, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/e4ef64b)

#### Features

- Vite DevTools 統合の追加
- rolldown 1.0.0-beta.46 へアップグレード

### v0.17.0

Release: https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/releases/tag/v0.17.0

#### Breaking Changes

- unconfig が configLoader から削除 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/9d6a758)
  - auto (デフォルト)、native、unrun の3択に
- CI 環境で failOnWarn がデフォルト有効 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/617, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/245e76c)
- Rolldown ネイティブ watcher に移行 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/329, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/1c4f845)
- ATTW profile 値 esmOnly → esm-only (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/85c10f314aabac62907917db1cc49c677343d013)

#### Features

- WatchPlugin の export
- write オプション追加
- format 単位でオプション上書き可能に
- build:done フックに chunks 情報追加
- rolldown 1.0.0-beta.53 へアップグレード


### v0.18.0

Release: https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/releases/tag/v0.18.0

#### Breaking Changes

  - copy オプションを https://github.com/vladshcherbin/rollup-plugin-copy#file の挙動に統一 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/e864bb2)
    - from に指定したパスの basename が to の下に配置される
    - 例: { from: 'src/css', to: 'dist' } → dist/css/ にコピー


### v0.19.0

Release: https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/releases/tag/v0.19.0

#### Breaking Changes

- debugLogs → debug にリネーム (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/bb4e74c)
- silent オプション削除 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/590156f)
- debug → devtools にリネーム、debug.devtools → devtools.ui (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/63e6f4f)
- exports 自動生成の変更:
  - pure ESM パッケージから main / module フィールドを自動削除 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/1684161)
  - types 自動付与は exports.legacy 有効時のみ (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/issues/685, https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/7be6bad)

#### Features

- CSS exports 生成 (css.splitting 無効時)
- rolldown 1.0.0-beta.59 へアップグレード
- migrate コマンドのモノレポ対応

### v0.20.0

Release: https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/releases/tag/v0.20.0

#### Breaking Changes

- dts.resolve オプション削除 (https://github.com/rolldown/tsdown/commit/16655bc)

#### Features

- レガシー CJS 警告の無効化オプション
- inlineOnly オプションの dts ファイルへの適用
- エントリに配列とオブジェクトの混在を許可
- rolldown 1.0.0-rc.1 へアップグレード

author: as51340
body:
## What

Replace the coarse `std::shared_mutex`-based locking in both vertex and edge vector indices with a 3-tier `utils::ResourceLock` (READ_ONLY / WRITE / UNIQUE). This enables concurrent writes via the
 WRITE tier while reserving UNIQUE for remove/resize operations. The GC cleanup strategy is changed from a full index scan (`RemoveObsoleteEntries`) to targeted removal (`RemoveVertices` /
`RemoveEdges`) called before skip-list entries are freed, and the serialization path now extracts data under a read lock and writes outside the lock.

## Why

Can't rely on deleted() solely to determine whether the key should be deleted and usearch doesn't allow for concurrent inserts and searches.

## How

- **`vector_index_utils.hpp`**: Moved `mg_vector_index_t` and `synchronized_mg_vector_index_t` (with `ResourceLock`) into this shared header. The `UpdateVectorIndex` template is generalized over
`SyncIndex` so both vertex and edge sync wrappers dispatch through the same happy-path (WRITE lock for adds) / hard-path (UNIQUE lock for remove+resize) logic. 

- **`vector_index.cpp`**: All `ReadLock()`/`MutableSharedLock()`/`Lock()` calls replaced with `SharedResourceLockGuard(READ_ONLY)` / `SharedResourceLockGuard(WRITE)` / `std::lock_guard` (UNIQUE).
`RemoveObsoleteEntries` replaced with `RemoveVertices(vector<Vertex*>)` using a two-phase approach: READ_ONLY to find which vertices exist in each index, then UNIQUE only on indices that need
removal. Serialization extracts keys+vectors under READ_ONLY into a local buffer, then writes to the encoder outside the lock.

- **`vector_edge_index.cpp`**: Same `ResourceLock` treatment. Defines a local `synchronized_mg_vector_edge_index_t` mirroring the vertex struct. `RemoveObsoleteEntries` replaced with
`RemoveEdges(list<Gid>)` — a two-phase approach that exports keys under READ_ONLY, filters by GID, then removes under UNIQUE. Fixed a bug where `GetVectorFromEdge` was taking an exclusive lock
instead of READ_ONLY.

- **`indices.cpp` / `indices.hpp`**: Removed `RemoveObsoleteEntries` calls from the periodic GC path. Added `RemoveVerticesFromVectorIndices` and `RemoveEdgesFromVectorEdgeIndices` as targeted GC
entry points.

- **`storage.cpp` (GC flow)**: Targeted removal is called in four places — both the transactional path (`current_deleted_vertices` / `current_deleted_edges` before skip-list removal) and the
`IN_MEMORY_ANALYTICAL` full-scan path (`need_full_scan_vertices` / `need_full_scan_edges` before skip-list removal). All guarded by `Empty()` checks to avoid unnecessary work when no vector
indices exist.

## Testing

**Unit tests** (`tests/unit/vector_edge_index.cpp`):
- Added `VectorEdgeIndexGCTest` fixture with periodic GC (100ms interval).
- `AnalyticalModeDeleteEdgeGCCleansVectorIndex`: Creates edge in transactional mode, switches to analytical, deletes, switches back (triggering GC), verifies index is cleaned.
- `AnalyticalModeDeleteMultipleEdgesGCCleansVectorIndex`: Deletes 2 of 3 edges in analytical mode, verifies only the surviving edge remains after GC.
- `TransactionalModeDeleteEdgeGCCleansVectorIndex`: Deletes edge in transactional mode, waits for periodic GC, verifies cleanup.
- Updated existing `RemoveEntriesTest` to use the new `RemoveEdges` API.

**Stress tests** (new workloads):
- `vector_index_concurrent_ops`: HA stress test with concurrent create/delete operations on vertex vector indices across multiple tenants, followed by restart and replica consistency checks.
- `vector_edge_index_recovery`: Same pattern for edge vector indices.

> ## Context
> A previous Copilot task/PR was merged prematurely and only completed "Explore existing codebase". The repository still needs the actual implementation.
> 
> Repo: `JMPawlicki/Chess_system`
> Base: `main`
> 
> ## Objective
> Implement the previously specified TCP pull-style integration between Python (DGT + chess legality + Stockfish) and MATLAB (robot + GUI), gating DGT input so robot moves are not interpreted.
> 
> ## Required changes
> ### 1) Preserve legacy script
> - Copy current `chess_system.py` to `chess_system_legacy.py` (unaltered except possibly a header comment noting legacy status).
> - Keep `chess_system.py` either as a thin wrapper/launcher or update it to new server behavior (choose the cleanest approach). Prefer creating a new entrypoint `brain_server.py` and leaving `chess_system.py` as legacy-compatible or a wrapper that calls `brain_server`.
> 
> ### 2) Create TCP server brain
> Add `brain_server.py` (or similarly named) that:
> - Opens TCP server on `127.0.0.1:5000`.
> - Uses line-based UTF-8 messages (`\n` terminated).
> - Handles commands (MATLAB -> Python):
>   - `CONFIG depth=<int> human=<white|black>`
>   - `NEW_GAME`
>   - `READY`
>   - `GET_BEST_MOVE`
>   - `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`
>   - `PROMOTE <q|r|b|n>`
>   - `SHUTDOWN`
> - Emits events/responses (Python -> MATLAB):
>   - `READY_OK`
>   - `HUMAN_MOVE <uci>`
>   - `BEST_MOVE <uci>`
>   - `PROMOTION_REQUIRED <uci_base>`
>   - `GAME_OVER <result>` (`1-0`, `0-1`, `1/2-1/2`)
>   - `ERROR <text>`
> 
> ### 3) Turn gating & state machine
> - DGT processing must be enabled **only** during human turns, after `READY`.
> - During engine/robot move and while waiting for `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`, ignore DGT input entirely.
> - Use Approach A:
>   - On `GET_BEST_MOVE`, compute engine move, force engine promotions to queen (`q`), store as `pending_engine_move`, send `BEST_MOVE ...`, but do not push to `chess.Board()`.
>   - On `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`, push `pending_engine_move` to board, update stockfish, then resume listening for human moves.
> - Add a debounce/quiet window after `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE` before accepting DGT again (e.g. 0.5s), ignoring incoming DGT segments.
> 
> ### 4) Promotions
> - Human promotions must not use `input()`.
> - When a human pawn reaches last rank, emit `PROMOTION_REQUIRED <uci_base>` and wait for `PROMOTE ...` to finalize and then emit `HUMAN_MOVE <uci_with_suffix>`.
> - Engine promotions always forced to queen.
> 
> ### 5) Hardcoded hardware configuration
> - Serial port: `COM6`, baud `38400`, timeout `0.3`.
> - Stockfish path: `./stockfish/stockfish-windows-x86-64-avx2.exe`.
> - No console prompts.
> 
> ### 6) Game end conditions
> - After pushing a human move or after applying the engine move on `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`, check for game end and emit `GAME_OVER ...`.
> - Treat threefold repetition / 50-move rule / insufficient material as immediate draw for simplicity.
> 
> ### 7) MATLAB example
> Add `matlab_client_example.m` demonstrating:
> - connecting to localhost:5000
> - sending `CONFIG`, `NEW_GAME`, `READY`
> - reading events
> - requesting `GET_BEST_MOVE` when appropriate
> - sending `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`
> - handling `PROMOTION_REQUIRED` by sending `PROMOTE q` (or prompting)
> 
> ### 8) Documentation
> Update README with:
> - how to run `brain_server.py`
> - protocol commands/events
> - how to run the MATLAB example
> - note about engine promotions always being queen
> 
> ## Acceptance criteria
> - Python brain can run headless (no stdin).
> - MATLAB can connect and complete one full cycle: receive `HUMAN_MOVE`, request `GET_BEST_MOVE`, receive `BEST_MOVE`, send `ENGINE_MOVE_DONE`.
> - DGT is ignored during robot move period.
>

> The previous task was canceled due to premature merge; this PR should contain all missing deliverables.

author: 0xnyk
body:
## Summary

Fixes three WebSocket disconnect bugs and adds SSE reconnect resilience. Also updates the README with all recently shipped features.

### WebSocket fixes
- **Stale closure in `onclose`**: reconnect now calls `connectRef.current` (a ref that always points to the latest `connect` function) instead of capturing `connect` by closure value. This was the most likely cause of users seeing broken reconnects after a few disconnects.
- **Disconnect-reconnect race**: `disconnect()` now sets `manualDisconnectRef = true` *before* calling `ws.close()`, so the async `onclose` handler skips auto-reconnect scheduling. Previously, a manual disconnect could accidentally trigger a new reconnect timer.
- **Double-connect guard**: now checks both `OPEN` and `CONNECTING` states. Previously only checked `OPEN`, allowing two connections to race when clicking reconnect while auto-reconnect was pending.

### SSE fixes
- **Exponential backoff**: replaces flat 3-second infinite retry with exponential backoff (1s → 30s max) and a 20-attempt cap
- **Error logging**: SSE errors are now logged with `console.warn` including attempt count (were previously silently swallowed)

### README updates
- Panel count: 26 → 28
- API route count: 64 → 66
- Migration count: 20 → 21
- E2E test count: 165 → 148 (was overstated)
- Added missing features: Agent SOUL system, Ed25519 device identity, agent messaging, update checker, workspace sync
- Added missing API routes to reference
- Added `NEXT_PUBLIC_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` to env vars table
- Updated roadmap with recently shipped items

## Proposed Changes

Replace the hardcoded `tls.VersionTLS13` in queue-proxy's TLS server with the shared `knative.dev/pkg/tls` package, allowing TLS settings to be configured via `QUEUE_PROXY_TLS_MIN_VERSION`, `QUEUE_PROXY_TLS_MAX_VERSION`,  `QUEUE_PROXY_TLS_CIPHER_SUITES`, and `QUEUE_PROXY_TLS_CURVE_PREFERENCES` environment variables. The default remains `TLS 1.3` when no env var is set.

Add four new keys to the config-deployment ConfigMap (`queue-sidecar-tls-min-version`, `queue-sidecar-tls-max-version`,
`queue-sidecar-tls-cipher-suites`, `queue-sidecar-tls-curve-preferences`) and forward them as `QUEUE_PROXY_TLS_*` environment variables in `makeQueueContainer`. This allows cluster admins to configure the queue-proxy's TLS server via the same ConfigMap used for other queue-proxy settings (like `queue-sidecar-rootca`), since the operator cannot inject env vars into the dynamically created sidecar via manifestival.

author: copilot
body:
Implements the baseline (non-optimising) JIT compiler that translates `BytecodeArray` to native x86-64 machine code, executing via `mmap`'d RWX memory. Each bytecode maps to a fixed native sequence; complex operations (property access, calls, closures) jump to a shared deopt epilogue returning `JIT_DEOPT`.

## MacroAssembler additions (`masm_x64.rs`)
- `CondCode` enum (`Equal`, `NotEqual`, `Less`, `LessEq`, `Greater`, `GreaterEq`)
- Memory: `mov_load_base_disp32` / `mov_store_base_disp32` — `[base + disp32]` with SIB handling for RSP/R12
- Arithmetic: `xor_rr`, `xor_ri`, `imul_rr`, `neg_r`, `test_rr`
- Conditional: `setcc_al`, `movzx_r64_al`, `jcc`

## Baseline compiler (`compiler/baseline/compiler.rs`)

**JIT value encoding** (`i64` per slot — disjoint from any `i32` Smi):
| JS value | `i64` |
|---|---|
| `Smi(v)` | `v as i64` |
| `true` | `0x1_0000_0001` |
| `false` | `0x1_0000_0000` |
| `undefined` / `null` | `0x1_0000_0002` / `0x1_0000_0003` |

**Register convention**: R12 = accumulator (callee-saved), R14 = register-file base (callee-saved, passed in RDI), R11 = scratch.

**Compiled opcodes** (direct native emission): `LdaZero/Smi/Undefined/Null/True/False/Constant`, `Ldar/Star/Mov`, `Add/Sub/Mul/Inc/Dec/AddSmi/SubSmi/MulSmi/Negate`, all `TestXxx` comparisons, `LogicalNot/ToBooleanLogicalNot`, all conditional and unconditional jump variants, `Return`.

**Deopt stubs**: property access, calls, closures, contexts, generators → jump to deopt epilogue → return `JIT_DEOPT = i64::MIN`.

**Metadata**: safepoint table (one entry per bytecode instruction) and deopt table (one entry per deoptimizing instruction).

```rust
// Compile and run via JIT, compare to interpreter
let compiled = BaselineCompiler::compile(&bytecode_array)?;
let jit_result = unsafe { compiled.execute(&[]) }?;
// jit_result is i64; use jit_to_jsvalue() to compare with JsValue from interpreter
```

**`CompiledCode::execute`** (x86-64 + Unix): allocates RWX memory via `mmap`, copies code, invokes `extern "C" fn(*mut i64) -> i64`, unmaps.

## Dependencies
- `libc = "0.2"` added as a platform-scoped dependency (`cfg(target_arch = "x86_64", unix)`) for `mmap`/`munmap`.

author: pawel-twardziak
body:
Both `RedisSaver.put()` and `ShallowRedisSaver.put()` unconditionally set `has_writes: "false"` when storing a checkpoint document. This is correct for the normal flow (put then putWrites), but breaks the interrupt flow where `putWrites()` is called *before* `put()`.

 In the interrupt flow, `putWrites` stores write data in Redis under a sorted set key (`write_keys_zset:...`). When `put()` runs afterwards and sets `has_writes: "false"`, the writes still exist in Redis but are invisible to `getTuple()` / `list()` because the RediSearch query filters on `has_writes == "true"`. This causes `pendingWrites` (including `__interrupt__` writes) to silently disappear.

The fix checks whether the write keys sorted set already exists in Redis before setting the `has_writes` flag, so pre-existing writes are preserved.

### Changes

- **`RedisSaver.put()`** (`index.ts`): check `client.exists()` on the write keys zset before building the checkpoint document
- **`ShallowRedisSaver.put()`** (`shallow.ts`): same fix
- **Integration tests** (`checkpoint.int.test.ts`): 6 new tests (3 per saver) covering putWrites-before-put, putWrites-after-put, and put-putWrites-put (double-put) scenarios

author: luisvmiranda
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a safer, local-first way to launch the Gradio demo with conservative defaults to avoid accidental public exposure or heavy GPU usage.
- Detect runtime capabilities (CUDA, CPU cores, RAM) and enforce sane runtime/thread settings before loading large models.
- Prefer CPU by default and avoid aggressive optimizations (no flash-attn) unless explicitly requested and available.

### Description
- Add `tools/launch_local_ui.py`, a small launcher that detects runtime capabilities via `torch` and `os` and prints staged logs such as `Setting up…`, `Downloading weights…`, `Loading model…`, and `Ready at <...>`.
- Use conservative defaults including `DEFAULT_CHECKPOINT = "Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-0.6B-CustomVoice"`, `max_new_tokens=1024`, CPU `dtype=float32` unless CUDA is selected and available, and `attn_implementation='sdpa'` (no flash-attn).
- Apply thread guardrails before model load by setting `OMP_NUM_THREADS` and `MKL_NUM_THREADS` to `min(8, os.cpu_count())` and calling `torch.set_num_threads(...)`.
- Bind to localhost only by probing for a free port starting at `8000` on `127.0.0.1`, enable Gradio queue with `default_concurrency_limit=1`, and auto-open the browser by preferring `launch(inbrowser=True)` with a polling fallback that uses `webbrowser.open(url)`.

### Testing
- Successfully compiled the new script with `python -m py_compile tools/launch_local_ui.py`.
- No other automated tests were modified or executed; the change is additive and does not alter existing CLI demo behavior (`qwen_tts/cli/demo.py`).

author: saanikaguptamicrosoft
body: ### Notes - This PR adds support for x-ms-correlation-request-id header propagation and switches the extension entrypoint to use azdext.Run. **azdext.Run is the new recommended approach-** - The previous entrypoint used context.Background(), which meant the extension had no awareness of the trace context from azd core. When azd launches an extension, it passes a TRACEPARENT environment variable containing the OpenTelemetry trace ID. azdext.Run calls NewContext() which reads this env var and injects the trace ID into the Go context — enabling end-to-end trace correlation. [[cp](https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/blob/7ebd9e09898cae5f42a4a92c449ab5f33775f4a8/cli/azd/pkg/azdext/context.go#L29)] - Replaced manual context.Background() + ExecuteContext + init() with azdext.Run, which handles FORCE_COLOR, TRACEPARENT injection, access token setup, and structured error reporting out of the box. One behavioral difference: errors now go to stderr (correct behavior) instead of stdout, and may include suggestion text for actionable errors. ### Testing - azd x build - Succeeds - Manual testing- - Added temporary changes for logging and to pick local azsdk changes: [commit1](https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/pull/6969/changes/857e74f1c030aa36cc11396d63547e5e3211ce6c), [commit2](https://github.com/Azure/azure-dev/pull/6969/changes/1880a1e1207dcab7c74091bc096231ca54b09f84) - Run go mod tidy - Confirmed that `x-ms-client-request-id` is being set:

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive coupon management module to the application. It includes all necessary backend logic, validation, and routing for creating, updating, deleting, validating, and fetching coupons, as well as integrating these routes into the main API. The changes ensure robust validation, tenant and role-based access control, and proper error handling for coupon operations.

**Coupon Module Implementation**

* Added a full-featured `coupon.controller.ts` with endpoints for creating, updating, deleting, validating, and fetching coupons, utilizing service layer logic and standard API response patterns.
* Implemented `coupon.service.ts` containing all core business logic for coupon management, including code uniqueness checks, tenant/restaurant scoping, validation rules (e.g., usage limits, date ranges, per-user limits), and discount calculation.
* Defined TypeScript types/interfaces for coupon creation, update, and validation payloads in `coupon.types.ts` for strong typing and clarity.

**Validation and Routing**

* Added `coupon.validation.ts` with Zod schemas to enforce input validation for all coupon endpoints, including checks for required fields, date logic, and enum constraints.
* Created `coupon.routes.ts` to define RESTful routes for coupon operations, applying appropriate middleware for authentication, tenant access, and validation; supports both customer and owner/manager roles.

**Integration and Configuration**

* Integrated the coupon routes into the main API router, making all coupon endpoints available under `/coupon`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4c1a276a826a5147689418cdbf9bde24c8326cedb30a61144fe7867bd99113efR7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4c1a276a826a5147689418cdbf9bde24c8326cedb30a61144fe7867bd99113efR44-R47)

body:
## Summary

Extract the shared K8s caching and discovery infrastructure into `pkg/k8score` so both Radar and skyhook-connector can use it without duplicating code.

**Layer 1 — Typed Cache:**
- `pkg/k8score.ResourceCache` with `CacheConfig` callback injection (OnChange, OnDrop, etc.)
- Both Radar and connector wrap this with thin singletons + app-specific callbacks

**Layer 2 — Dynamic Cache + Discovery:**
- `pkg/k8score.DynamicResourceCache` with per-GVR sync tracking, parallel warmup, CRD discovery
- `pkg/k8score.ResourceDiscovery` with GVR resolution, CRD detection, watch-capability checking
- `StripUnstructuredFields` utility for removing managedFields/last-applied-configuration
- Radar's `internal/k8s` wrappers reduced to thin singletons over k8score

**Design pattern:** `pkg/k8score` has ZERO `internal/` imports. All app-specific behavior (timeline recording, metrics tracking, etc.) injected via config struct callbacks.

**Companion PR:** skyhook-dev/skyhook-connector — same branch, migrates connector to use the shared caches (deletes ~934 lines of duplicated cache code).

author: copilot
body:
Queue processor exited as soon as `pending == 0` regardless of how many jobs were still `RUNNING`, causing analysis to start with only 12/54 jobs complete. Result collection mapped all variants to the same model due to a wrong queue field lookup. Also implements the remaining items from FINAL_PR_SUMMARY.md.

## Bug fix: `process_queue_simple.py`

The termination condition only checked `pending_count == 0`. After `update_running_jobs_status()`, `running_count` was never recomputed, so 42 in-flight jobs were invisible to the exit check.

```python
# Before — exits immediately when nothing left to submit
if pending_count == 0:
    break

# After — waits for all running jobs to drain too
if pending_count == 0 and running_count == 0:
    break
elif pending_count == 0 and running_count > 0:
    time.sleep(RUNNING_JOBS_POLL_INTERVAL)  # 30s
    continue
```

## Bug fix: `analyze_benchmark_results.py`

`map_variants_to_timestamps()` was reading `entry.get("gcs_prefix")` — a field that `process_queue_simple.py` never writes. This caused `timestamp_map` to always be empty, so every variant fell back to the same most-recent `model_summary.json`, producing identical metrics for all variants in the CSV (same `model_id` for every row).

Fixed to read fields in priority order:
1. `timestamp` — written by `process_queue_simple.py` at job launch
2. `expected_result_path` — parse last path segment
3. `gcs_prefix` — legacy fallback for backward compatibility

Also accepts `RUNNING` entries in addition to `COMPLETED` so results can be read while jobs are still in-flight.

## New run modes: `run_full_benchmark.py`

Replaces the `is_test_run` boolean with a `run_mode` enum and adds two new mutually-exclusive CLI flags:

| Flag | Iterations × Trials | Est. time | Est. cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| _(default)_ | 10 × 1 | ~1-2 h | ~$10 |
| `--full-run` | 1000 × 3 | ~4-6 h | ~$75 |
| `--extended-run` | 2000 × 5 | ~10-15 h | ~$220 |
| `--production-run` | 5000 × 5 | ~25-35 h | ~$500 |

## Top-N combination selection: `benchmark_mmm.py`

New `--top-n {5,10,54}` flag (both scripts) backed by `select_top_combinations()`, which round-robins slots across adstock types then fills remaining slots in order — ensuring adstock diversity at any N.

## Documentation consolidation

- Merged `QUICK_START_GUIDE.md` → `README.md` (prerequisites, all run modes, cost table)
- Merged `DEBUGGING_GUIDE.md` → `USAGE_GUIDE.md` (Advanced Troubleshooting section)
- Deleted both source files — now 5 essential docs instead of 7

Refactored the final writeback in `pppRandUpChar` to branch directly on `sourceOffset` at the point of update, instead of storing a precomputed target pointer.

- Symbol: `pppRandUpChar`

This keeps behavior identical and reads like source-authored gameplay code: update the global fallback color slot when `sourceOffset == -1`, otherwise update the computed object-relative slot. - Moved source-offset branching from pointer selection into the final writeback block.

author: magnetised
body:
Running locally I've seen errors collecting the statistics for the number of shapes and sqlite metrics because the telemetry poller runs before the shape db has properly started.

This pr adds an arbitrary delay to the start of metrics collection to make that situation less likely. 

It also simplifies the db optimization process by always checking out a connection from the write pool even in non-exclusive mode, rather than maintaining a separate persistent connection just for the periodic optimize call.

### Motivation

- Consolidate and harden the web API auth verification logic to avoid accidental bypass when `auth_key` is missing and to mitigate timing attacks.

### Description

- Extracted the auth validation logic into a new function `isValidAuthKey` and replaced the inline logic in `Prepare` to call it.
- Implemented constant-time comparison using `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` and explicit checks for empty inputs and timestamp window (20 seconds).
- Removed the previous fallback that generated a random `configKey` when the configured `auth_key` was empty, so an empty `auth_key` no longer implicitly enables auth.
- Added unit tests in `web/controllers/base_test.go` covering a valid case and several invalid scenarios (`empty key`, `expired timestamp`, `length mismatch`, `wrong key`, and `empty config key`).

### Testing

- Ran the controller package tests with `go test ./web/controllers`, and the new tests `TestIsValidAuthKey` and `TestIsValidAuthKeyInvalidCases` passed.

author: 0keith
body:
## Summary
Implements automatic installation to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PaperNexus\` on first run and adds inter-process communication (IPC) to signal the running instance to show the UI when a second instance starts.

## Key Changes

- **Auto-Install on First Run:** When the executable runs from outside the install directory, `Program.Main` now:
  - Detects if running from the install location by comparing full paths
  - If not installed, checks if an installed instance is already running
  - If running, signals it to show UI and exits
  - If not running, copies the exe to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PaperNexus\`, migrates `settings.json` and `timers.json` if present, and relaunches from the install location
  - Handles file lock errors gracefully by launching the existing copy if available

- **IPC Event Handle for Show UI:** Replaces silent exit behavior with active signaling:
  - Introduces a named `EventWaitHandle` (`PaperNexus_ShowUI`) for cross-instance communication
  - When a second instance detects the mutex is held, it signals the running instance to show the UI instead of silently exiting
  - The primary instance creates and monitors the event handle on a background thread
  - Properly disposes the event handle in a finally block

- **App UI Signaling:** `App.axaml.cs` now:
  - Monitors the `ShowUIEvent` on a background thread with a 1-second timeout
  - Calls `ShowMainWindow()` when signaled by a second instance
  - Gracefully handles `ObjectDisposedException` during shutdown

- **Default Download Folder:** Changed from `~/wallpapers` to `~/Pictures/PaperNexus` for better UX alignment with standard Windows picture storage conventions

- **Documentation:** Updated `CLAUDE.md` to reflect the new auto-install and IPC behavior

author: omraanz
body:
## Summary
Extended the document retriever node to support both PostgreSQL (local development) and Databricks (development/staging) backends, enabling seamless operation across different database environments without code changes.

## Key Changes

- **Unified query interface**: Created `_execute_query()` function that abstracts database operations and routes to either PostgreSQL or Databricks based on `DB_BACKEND` configuration
- **Databricks SQL connector**: Added lazy-loaded Databricks connection management with `_get_databricks_connection()` for efficient resource handling
- **Dynamic table name support**: Replaced hardcoded `metadata_gcpl` references with configurable `METADATA_TABLE_NAME` from environment, supporting both local and development table schemas
- **Expanded metadata columns**: Added support for additional filterable columns (`file_sub_category_det`, `product_sub_category_det`, `sub_brand_variant_det`, `region_det`) to match development environment schema
- **Improved result formatting**: Extracted formatting logic into `_format_results()` function with enhanced markdown output (tables for 3+ results with metadata, numbered lists for sparse data)
- **Graceful column discovery**: Modified `_fetch_distinct_column_values()` to skip unavailable columns per environment rather than failing entirely
- **Dynamic tool documentation**: Tool docstring now generated at runtime to reflect the configured table name and available columns
- **Configuration management**: Added `.env.example` with all required environment variables and updated `config.py` with new backend/table settings

## Implementation Details

- Database routing is transparent to the rest of the pipeline — the node automatically uses the configured backend
- Databricks connection is created once and reused (singleton pattern) to minimize overhead
- Column availability is detected at module load time and cached, allowing graceful degradation if columns don't exist in a particular environment
- Result formatting intelligently chooses between table and list layouts based on result count and metadata richness
- All hardcoded table/column references replaced with configuration-driven values for portability

body:
# Refactor Runs API to Implement Lazy Loading for Heavy Output Fields

## Problem

The `/runs` endpoint previously returned full run records including large fields:
- `serializableOutput`
- `binaryOutput`

This caused:
- Large API payload sizes
- Slow dashboard initial render
- Increased memory consumption
- Poor scalability for users with many runs

## Solution

Implemented a lazy-loading architecture:

### 1. Optimized `/runs`
- Now returns metadata only
- Explicitly excludes heavy output fields
- Ordered by `startedAt DESC`

### 2. Introduced `/runs/:runId/output`
- Returns only:
  - `serializableOutput`
  - `binaryOutput`
- Intended for UI expansion use-case

### 3. Bug Fix
- Corrected incorrect parameter reference in `/runs/run/:id`

## Architectural Improvement

This separates:
- Run metadata (list view)
- Run output payload (detail view)

Benefits:
- Reduced initial payload size
- Improved dashboard responsiveness
- More scalable for high-volume users
- Cleaner API contract separation

## Backward Compatibility

- No changes to run execution flow
- No changes to data schema
- Full run retrieval still supported via `/runs/run/:id`

## Backward Compatibility

- No breaking changes
- Run execution flow unchanged

Closes #989

author: hilaryduffrules-hash
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several real bugs that affect core functionality, adds keyboard typing mode alongside voice, and improves accessibility and mobile handling — all while keeping the privacy-first, local-only architecture intact.

---

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

### Critical: Speech transcript concatenated without spaces (App.tsx)
The original code joined all speech recognition segments with `''.join('')`:
```js
// Before — 'hello' + 'world' = 'helloworld'
.join('')

// After — trims each segment, joins with space
.map((r) => r[0].transcript.trim()).filter(Boolean).join(' ')
```
This caused the word-matching logic to almost never fire correctly when the recognizer split the transcript across multiple segments (which happens on any pause in speech).

### Critical: Stale closure on latestRef (App.tsx)
`latestRef` was updated inside a `useEffect`, which runs asynchronously *after* paint. A speech recognition result arriving in that window would call the old `handleSpeechInput` with stale `quote` state — causing it to match against the previous quote.

Fixed by updating `latestRef.current` directly in the render function body (synchronous, no effect needed). React refs are safe to write during render.

### TypeScript error: onInputChange required but never passed (TypingArea.tsx)
`onInputChange` was a required prop in the interface but `App.tsx` never passed it. Added `?` to make it optional. Added companion `onKeystroke?` for per-keystroke accuracy.

### cursor-blink animation never fired (TypingArea.tsx + index.html)
The CSS declared `@keyframes blink` but the class was `cursor-blink`. Name mismatch meant the cursor never blinked. Fixed by renaming to `@keyframes cursor-blink` and changing `border-color` to `inherit` so it works with both dark and light theme border colours (was hardcoded to `#0071e3`).

### WPM could produce NaN or Infinity (App.tsx)
The WPM `useEffect` ran immediately when `status` changed to `RUNNING`, before any time had elapsed, producing `0 / 0 = NaN`. Added a `timeElapsedMin <= 0` guard.

### recognition.stop() could throw on reset (App.tsx)
`resetTest` called `recognitionRef.current.stop()` without a try/catch. If recognition had already ended (e.g. silence timeout), this would throw an uncaught exception. Wrapped in try/catch.

---

## ✨ New Features

### Keyboard typing mode (⌨️ Keys)
Added a Voice / Keys toggle in the nav. Keyboard mode:
- Renders a hidden `<input>` inside `TypingArea` that captures keystrokes on all platforms including mobile (with `autoComplete off`, `autoCorrect off`, `autoCapitalize off`, `enterKeyHint='next'`).
- Auto-focuses the input when the test starts so users don't need to click anything.
- Clicking anywhere in the text area re-focuses the input if it loses focus.
- Tracks per-keystroke accuracy via `onKeyDown` (before the value changes), so backspace-corrected errors are still counted.
- Advances to the next quote automatically when the full text is matched exactly.

### Real accuracy tracking in keyboard mode
Accuracy = (correct keystrokes / total keystrokes) × 100, updated live. Voice mode continues to show 100% which is correct by design (only exact word matches advance the cursor).

### Richer results card
Final results now show: Speed (WPM), Accuracy, Words typed, Characters typed, and Error count (keyboard) / mode icon (voice).

### WPM color coding in StatsOverlay
- 🔴 < 30 WPM
- 🟡 30–59 WPM
- 🟢 ≥ 60 WPM

### Formatted time display
Durations ≥ 60 s now show as `M:SS` (e.g. `1:02`) instead of a bare second count.

---

## ♿ Accessibility

- `aria-pressed` on mode and duration toggle buttons.
- `role='status'` + `aria-live='polite'` on the stats overlay.
- Individual `aria-label` on each stat value.
- `role='region'` + `aria-label` on the typing area.
- `aria-label` on dark/light toggle, start button, and listening indicator.
- SVG icons marked `aria-hidden='true'`.

---

## 📱 Mobile

- `touch-action: manipulation` on all buttons — eliminates 300 ms tap delay and prevents accidental double-tap zoom.
- `-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%` prevents iOS from inflating font sizes on landscape rotation.
- Hidden keyboard input uses mobile-friendly attributes (`autoCapitalize`, `enterKeyHint`, etc.).
- Nav wraps on small screens via `flex-wrap`.

---

## 🏷️ Branding / Meta

- Rename title from `SwiftVoice` → `SwiftType` (consistent with repo name and project intent).
- Update OG, Twitter, and JSON-LD descriptions to mention both modes and privacy-first local processing.
- Footer updated: replaces generic tagline with *'Privacy-first. No data leaves your browser.'*

---

## Privacy

No changes to the privacy model. All speech recognition uses the browser-native Web Speech API. No data is sent to any external service. The keyboard path is fully local.

## P0: Create Market UX Fixes

Three bugs reported by Khubair on the Create Market flow.

### Bug 1: Quick Launch broken
**Problem:** Auto oracle detect wasn't advancing — user forced to go Manual > HyperpEMA > select market type manually.

**Fix:** Added auto-advance effects in `CreateMarketWizard`:
- Step 1 → Step 2: auto-advances once token is resolved and quick launch params are ready
- Step 2 → Step 4: auto-advances once oracle is resolved (Pyth/HyperpEMA/Admin)
- Steps 2 & 3 are skipped entirely in Quick mode — user goes from Token → Review

### Bug 2: No devnet token minting at Step 4
**Problem:** No way to mint devnet tokens. Post-creation `/api/devnet-mint-token` call used stale `state.slabAddress` (captured before setState updates), so it was called with `null`.

**Fix:**
- Changed to use `slabPk.toBase58()` directly (not the stale state closure)
- API response (devnetMint, airdropAmount, symbol) now stored in `CreateMarketState`
- `LaunchSuccess` shows airdrop confirmation (✓ Airdropped X tokens)
- StepReview shows "Mint Devnet Tokens →" link when user has no tokens on devnet

### Bug 3: CA mismatch UX
**Problem:** Devnet mint CA differs from mainnet CA user pasted. No indication of this.

**Fix:** `LaunchSuccess` now shows:
- ⚠️ "Devnet uses a different mint address" notice
- Mainnet CA and Devnet CA side-by-side
- Copy button for devnet mint address
- Explanation of what to use when trading

### Files Changed
- `app/components/create/CreateMarketWizard.tsx` — auto-advance effects, pass new props
- `app/components/create/LaunchSuccess.tsx` — devnet mint info, CA comparison, airdrop confirmation
- `app/components/create/StepReview.tsx` — mint address display, devnet token guide link
- `app/hooks/useCreateMarket.ts` — new state fields, fixed stale closure bug

author: workjaykanzariya-byte
body:
### Motivation
- Zoho webhook deliveries use an `X-Webhook-Token` header and vary payload shapes, which caused valid payment/subscription events to be rejected or mis-parsed and prevented users' membership fields from being updated.
- The webhook endpoint must be resilient to header case, stringified JSON payloads, and multiple event keys so membership updates are applied reliably on successful payments.

### Description
- Updated `ZohoWebhookController::handle` to read `X-Webhook-Token` (case-insensitive), compare it to `config('zoho_billing.webhook_secret')`, log unauthorized attempts with IP/headers, and return `401` when the header is missing or mismatched.
- Hardened webhook payload parsing by using `$request->all()` with a raw JSON fallback and added logging of `event_type`, `event_id`, keys, and a safe raw preview, and the controller now always returns `200` (with `handled` flag) for valid-token deliveries to avoid retry storms on parsing errors.
- Enhanced `ZohoBillingService::applyWebhookEvent()` to accept `event_type` or `eventType`, accept `payload` or `data`, decode stringified JSON payloads, handle extra paid events (`invoice_paid`, `payment_success`) in addition to existing ones, normalize plan/starts/ends fields, and keep warnings when a user cannot be resolved by customer/subscription ids.
- Added an authenticated backup endpoint `GET /api/v1/billing/hostedpages/{hostedpageId}/sync` and controller action `BillingCheckoutController::syncHostedPage` to fetch the hosted page and run `syncMembershipFromHostedPage()` for manual reconciliation; added the route in `routes/api.php`.

### Testing
- Ran PHP lint (`php -l`) on the modified files (`app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/Zoho/ZohoWebhookController.php`, `app/Support/Zoho/ZohoBillingService.php`, `app/Http/Controllers/Api/V1/Billing/BillingCheckoutController.php`, `routes/api.php`) and all returned "No syntax errors detected." (success).
- Attempted to inspect routes via `php artisan route:list` but it failed in this environment due to missing composer dependencies (`vendor/autoload.php`), so runtime route verification could not be completed here (environment limitation).
