author: copilot
body:
Deployment of the analytics/calendar/review features introduced three compounding issues causing a 500 on every page load.

## Root causes & fixes

### `/_not-found` prerender crash (primary 500 source)
`global-not-found.tsx` was never picked up by Next.js — the file must be exactly `not-found.tsx`. The original also had nested `<html>`/`<body>` inside a layout-wrapped route and was missing `force-dynamic`, causing the build to attempt static prerendering of `/_not-found` with `ClerkProvider` present, which throws at build time without a publishable key.

Created `src/app/not-found.tsx` — correct filename, no nested html/body, `force-dynamic` export.

### Dashboard pages missing `force-dynamic`
`/dashboard` and `/dashboard/provider` call `auth()` and query the DB at request time. Next.js was trying to statically prerender both at build time and failing.

Added `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` to both pages.

### Missing Prisma indexes for `relationMode = "prisma"`
With `relationMode = "prisma"`, every FK field needs an explicit `@@index` or Prisma cannot efficiently enforce relation constraints. Four were absent — two on `CallSheetItem` and two on `Review` — causing the new review queries to degrade and potentially fail on the new tables.

```prisma
model CallSheetItem {
  @@index([listingId])   // added
  @@index([serviceId])   // added
}

model Review {
  @@index([targetUserId])  // added
  @@index([authorId])      // added
}
```

### Auto schema sync on Coolify deploy
The new indexes and `Review` table would never land in production without manual shell access into the container. Added `prisma db push` to the build script so schema changes apply automatically on every Coolify redeploy — without `--accept-data-loss`, so any destructive change aborts the build rather than silently dropping data.

```json
"build": "prisma generate && prisma db push && next build && ..."
```

Closes #3133

Adds an optional autosave feature that automatically saves your work after you stop making changes. Helps prevent data loss without being intrusive.

**What it does:**
- New "Autosave interval" setting in Preferences → General → Saving and Loading
- Options: Disabled (default), 1/5/10/15/30/60 minutes
- Only saves after you stop editing for the specified time (debouncing)
- Works for maps, tilesets, and worlds

**Why debouncing:**
The timer restarts with each change, so it only saves after you've been idle for the full interval. This avoids interrupting your workflow with constant saves while still protecting your work.

**What it won't do:**
- Won't save untitled files (you need to save them once first)
- Won't save read-only files
- Won't create backup/recovery files (that's a different feature)

**Since this feature can be customized a lot, I am open for discussions and more ideas :)**

body:
### Motivation
- Allow clients to request distinct column values scoped to a specific event using an `event_name` parameter so property value suggestions can be limited per event. 
- Keep backward compatibility by falling back to the global `events_normalized` table when no `event_name` is provided or when the scoped table is missing.

### Description
- Extended the backend `GET /column-values` endpoint to accept an optional `event_name` query parameter and validate the requested column against either `events_scoped` or `events_normalized` as appropriate. 
- When `event_name` is provided the endpoint queries `events_scoped` (with parameterized SQL) and verifies the event exists, otherwise it queries `events_normalized`; when `events_scoped` is missing the global table is used for validation and values. 
- Updated the frontend API to accept an `eventName` argument in `getColumnValues` and to build the query string accordingly. 
- Updated `CohortForm` to request and cache column values per `(event_name, column)` using a composed cache key, and to disable value inputs until an event is selected.
- Added backend tests for scoped behavior in `backend/tests/test_scope.py` to cover scoped queries, global fallback, and validation against missing `events_scoped` table.

author: copilot
body:
Bot containers for `personal-biographer`, `diary`, and `journaler` were hard-coded in `_bots.html`. These are now constructed dynamically in `bots.mjs` based on `mBots` module data, eliminating the coupling between server-returned bot data and static HTML.

## `_bots.html`
- Removed `personal-biographer`, `diary`, and `journaler` bot container markup
- Retained required hard-coded elements: `team-popup`, `personal-avatar`, `team-header`, `collections-container`

## `bots.mjs`

**New/updated functions:**
- `mCreateBotContainer(bot)` — builds full bot container DOM using `bot.id` (uuid) for all element IDs; reads `bot.icon`, `bot.buttons`, `bot.options`, and `bot.retirable` directly from bot data instead of hardcoded switch-cases or static arrays
- `mBotInterestsContainer(botId, optionGroup)` — builds checkbox UI from a `bot.options[]` entry; uses `botId` (uuid) as element ID prefix and option item IDs from the server data
- `mCreateRetireContainer(id)` — builds retire chat/bot controls; now takes bot uuid instead of type string
- `mUpdateBotContainers()` — creates containers for any non-proxy, non-avatar bot in `mBots` that has no existing DOM element (keyed by `bot.id`) before updating all containers
- `mUpdateBotContainerAddenda()` — all sub-element lookups use `botContainer.id` (uuid) as prefix; button lookups use `querySelector('.routine-button')` / `querySelector('.bot-start')` instead of type-based IDs
- `mSetStatusBar()`, `mSetAttributes()`, `mUpdateInterests()`, `mSpotlightBotStatus()`, `setActiveBot()`, `mBotNameChange()` — updated to resolve elements via `botContainer.id` (uuid) rather than `type`, with fallbacks to type-based IDs for the hard-coded `personal-avatar` container

**Key design decisions:**
- All dynamically created bot container DOM IDs use the bot's uuid (`bot.id`), e.g. `${id}-status`, `${id}-icon`, `${id}-input-bot_name`
- `bot.buttons` entries use their own uuid (`button.id`) as DOM IDs and are sorted by `button.order`; `button.type` maps to CSS classes (`routine-button`, `bot-start`)
- `bot.options` checkbox groups are built entirely from server data; no static interest arrays remain in the module
- Hard-coded `personal-avatar` HTML retains its `personal-avatar-*` element IDs; downstream functions fall back to type-based lookup where needed

```js
// mUpdateBotContainers now inserts missing containers before updating (keyed by bot.id)
mBots
    .filter(bot => !globals.isProxy(bot.type))
    .forEach(bot => {
        const { id, type } = bot
        if (type === 'avatar' || type === 'personal-avatar') return
        if (!document.getElementById(id)) {
            const botContainer = mCreateBotContainer(bot)
            collectionsContainer.parentNode.insertBefore(botContainer, collectionsContainer)
        }
    })
```

body:
- Generates anonymous names (e.g. "Anonymous Capybara") from session IDs so video owners can see when non-authenticated users view their videos - Deduplicates notifications per session using a hashed session ID - Respects existing "pause views" notification preference - Merges anonymous view counts into the existing "Views" filter tab in the dashboard

Greptile Summary

This PR introduces anonymous view notifications, allowing video owners to see when non-authenticated users view their videos. It adds a new `anon_view` notification type backed by SHA-256-based dedup keys, DB-level rate limiting (50 per video per 5 min), a `firstViewEmailSentAt` sentinel column, and updated notification UI merging anonymous views into the "Views" tab. **Implementation approach:** - **`anonymous-names.ts`**: Uses `crypto.createHash('sha256')` for both display names and dedup hashing (fixes prior 32-bit collision risk). - **`Notification.ts` / `track/route.ts`**: DB-backed rate limiting (cross-instance safe), `revalidatePath` called after insert, `sendFirstViewEmail` supports both authenticated and anonymous viewers with preference checks. - **Database migrations 0013–0016**: All schema additions (`dedupKey`, `firstViewEmailSentAt`, indexes) are present and properly migrated. - **Dashboard UI**: `anon_view` merged into "Views" count via `matchNotificationFilter`. **Two user-facing logic bugs remain:** 1. **Anonymous owner self-notification**: When a logged-out video owner views their own video, the authenticated-owner guard doesn't fire (userId is null), allowing `createAnonymousViewNotification` and `sendFirstViewEmail` to run. Owner receives "Anonymous [Animal] viewed your video" notification and "just got its first view!" email about their own anonymous view. 2. **Preference-blocked sentinel**: When `pauseAnonViews` or `pauseViews` is true, `sendFirstViewEmail` returns early without setting `firstViewEmailSentAt`. Later, when the preference is toggled back on, the next viewer's notification triggers a retroactively inaccurate "just got its first view!" email.

Confidence Score: 2/5

- Two correctness bugs will produce incorrect user-facing behavior: video owners will receive spurious notifications about their own anonymous views, and first-view emails will fire retroactively for later viewers when notification preferences are toggled. - The implementation of anonymous view notifications is architecturally sound — DB-backed deduplication, SHA-256 hashing, cross-instance rate limiting, and proper schema migration are all correct. However, two user-facing logic errors remain unresolved: (1) owners viewing while logged out receive notifications/emails about their own views because the owner-bypass guard doesn't catch null userId, and (2) when notification preferences pause anonymous/authenticated views, the `firstViewEmailSentAt` sentinel is never set, causing the "first view" email to fire retroactively for a much-later viewer after the preference is toggled back on. Both bugs will be visible to users and should be fixed before deployment. - apps/web/app/api/analytics/track/route.ts (owner bypass for logged-out case) and apps/web/lib/Notification.ts (sentinel timing relative to preference checks).

## Summary
This PR adds two new pages for advanced F1 statistics and fastest lap tracking, enhances race detail pages with sprint results and pit stop analysis, and improves the driver/team comparison experience with visual charts.

## Key Changes

### New Pages
- **Stats Page** (`/stats`): Comprehensive season statistics including:
  - Season summary KPIs (races completed, total points, DNFs, driver count)
  - Positions gained/lost analysis with biggest single-race gains and losses
  - Points per race (PPR) leaderboard
  - Team DNF breakdown and reliability metrics
  - Laps led statistics
  - Overtakes per race tracking

- **Fastest Laps Page** (`/fastest-laps`): Dedicated fastest lap tracking with:
  - Driver leaderboard showing fastest lap count per driver
  - Fastest lap of the season highlight card
  - Race-by-race fastest lap table with lap times, speeds, and race positions
  - Links to individual race pages

### Enhanced Race Details
- Added Sprint Race Results table showing sprint race positions, grid, laps, and points
- Added Pit Stop Analysis section with:
  - Fastest pit stop highlight
  - Pit stops per driver grouped display
  - Average pit stop duration statistics

### Improved Comparisons & Visualizations
- Added Points Progression chart to driver comparison page showing cumulative points over the season
- Added Qualifying head-to-head (H2H) stats to comparison page
- Added Constructor Points Progression chart component for team standings visualization

### Driver Profile Enhancements
- Integrated official F1 driver number logos with fallback to styled text
- Added Position Trajectory sparkline showing driver's finishing positions across races
- Enhanced driver number display with proper styling

### UI/UX Improvements
- Enhanced dashboard with season progress bar for races completed
- Improved championship leader card with points gap to second place
- Added race result summaries (winner, pole, fastest lap) to race cards
- Enhanced navigation with new "Fastest Laps" and "Stats" menu items

### Data & API
- Added `getSprintResults()` and `getPitStops()` API functions

### Component Additions
- `ConstructorPointsChart`: SVG-based chart showing cumulative constructor points progression

- Stats calculations use efficient Map-based aggregation for performance
- Charts use SVG for responsive, lightweight visualization
- Pit stop analysis includes duration sorting and driver grouping

author: foxeeek
body:
### Motivation
- Newly published Freelancehunt projects could be missed because the scraper only read the single `/projects` listing page, and fast churn on page 1 meant new items were not always visible to the running scraper.
- There was risk of mismatched `external_id` comparisons (string vs. other types / whitespace) leading to false positives when checking DB deduplication.
- The scheduler and analysis flow could run into `NoneType` errors when analysis returned `None` and could use clearer, structured telemetry for the fetch cycle.
- The intent is to minimally fix detection and harden processing without redesigning architecture or adding new features.

### Description
- Added minimal pagination to Freelancehunt scraper by introducing `MAX_PAGES = 2` and fetching `?page=1..2`, keeping cross-page deduplication via a `seen_ids` set and preserving `external_id` extraction from the URL path segment in `freelance_ai/platforms/freelancehunt/scraper.py`.
- Normalized `external_id` before DB lookups and inserts by using `external_id = str(order_in.external_id).strip()` in `OrderService.upsert_order` to ensure consistent comparisons and storage in `freelance_ai/services/order_service.py`.
- Prevented `NoneType` crashes by adding a defensive guard in `OrderService.save_analysis` to return early if `analysis is None` in `freelance_ai/services/order_service.py`.
- Hardened scheduler processing in `freelance_ai/services/scheduler.py` by pre-normalizing orders, pre-checking existing `(platform, external_id)` rows in the DB to compute `Already in DB` and `New detected`, adding per-order `try/except` isolation, and emitting structured fetch-cycle logs including `Total parsed from page`, `Already in DB`, `New detected`, and a final per-platform summary `total_fetched`, `total_parsed`, `filtered_by_category`, `new_stored`, and `sent_to_telegram`.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall freelance_ai` and compilation succeeded for the package modules.
- Performed a runtime fetch smoke attempt with `asyncio.run(fetch_projects())`, but the environment raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sqlalchemy'` which blocked a full end-to-end run; the scraper code was exercised during development and logs were added to aid verification in production where dependencies are present.
- No automated unit tests exist in the repository; changes were kept minimal and safe to make manual validation straightforward (observe new scheduler logs and scraper per-page logs in production runs).

author: kshyju
body:
### Motivation and Context

   The Agent Framework needs support for long-running, reliable agent orchestrations that can survive process restarts, scale across machines, and handle complex multi-step workflows. This PR brings durable workflow support backed by the Durable Task framework, enabling scenarios like multi-agent pipelines,  fan-out/fan-in patterns, and human-in-the-loop approvals.

   ### Description

   This PR merges the `feat/durable_task` feature branch, adding comprehensive durable workflow support across two packages. The feature was developed across 5 PRs into the feature branch:

   - **Basic durable workflow support** ([#3648](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/3648)) — Core workflow engine including `IWorkflowClient`, `IWorkflowRun`, `DurableWorkflowRunner`, `DurableWorkflowContext`, edge routers (direct and fan-out), activity executors, workflow analyzer, and streaming
   support via `IStreamingWorkflowRun`.

   - **Azure Functions hosting** ([#3935](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/3935)) — Hosting layer for running durable workflows in Azure Functions, including `WorkflowOrchestrator`, `DurableWorkflowsFunctionMetadataTransformer`, and DI extensions.

   - **Events & shared state** ([#4020](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4020)) — Support for publishing and subscribing to workflow events, and sharing state across workflow executors.

   - **Nested sub-workflows** ([#4190](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4190)) — Ability to compose workflows by nesting sub-workflows within a parent workflow.

   - **Human-in-the-loop (HITL)** ([#4358](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/pull/4358)) — Support for pausing workflow execution to wait for human input, including `DurableWorkflowWaitingForInputEvent`, `PendingRequestPortStatus`, and `DurableHaltRequestedEvent`.

   **Packages changed:**

   | Package | Files changed | Diff |
   |---------|--------------|------|
   | `Microsoft.Agents.AI.DurableTask` | 49 | +4,488 / −318 |
   | `Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.AzureFunctions` | 12 | +778 / −51 |

   **Key new types:**

   - `IWorkflowClient` / `DurableWorkflowClient` — Client for starting and managing workflow runs
   - `IWorkflowRun` / `IStreamingWorkflowRun` — Handles for monitoring workflow execution
   - `DurableWorkflowRunner` — Core orchestration runner
   - `DurableWorkflowContext` — Execution context available to workflow steps
   - `DurableExecutorDispatcher` — Routes execution to registered executors
   - `IDurableEdgeRouter` — Abstraction for routing between workflow nodes (direct, fan-out)
   - `WorkflowAnalyzer` / `WorkflowGraphInfo` — Static analysis of workflow graphs
   - `WorkflowOrchestrator` — Azure Functions orchestrator for durable workflows

   ### Contribution Checklist

   - [x] The code builds clean without any errors or warnings
   - [x] The PR follows the [Contribution Guidelines](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-framework/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
   - [x] All unit tests pass, and I have added new tests where possible

body:
# Pull Request

## Description
This PR adds multi-chain EVM support by making all DefraDB collection names configurable per chain, instead of being hard-coded to `Ethereum__Mainnet`. The indexer, schema, block handler, and pruner now derive collection/type names from a chain prefix based on config or environment variables.

## Changes
- Add `chain` section to config (`ChainConfig` with `name` and `network`), including defaults (`Ethereum` / `Mainnet`) and `CHAIN_NAME` / `CHAIN_NETWORK` env overrides.
- Introduce `CollectionNames` and `DefaultCollectionPrefix` in `constants` for generating chain-specific collection names (e.g. `Arbitrum__Mainnet__Block`) while keeping existing `constants.Collection*` and `constants.AllCollections` for backward compatibility.
- Extend schema handling with `GetSchemaForChain`, which rewrites the embedded GraphQL schema’s `Ethereum__Mainnet__*` types to the configured chain prefix.
- Update `BlockHandler` to hold a `*CollectionNames` and use it for all DefraDB collection accesses (including batch creation, batch signatures, and highest-block queries).
- Update `ChainIndexer` to:
  - Construct per-chain `CollectionNames` from config.
  - Apply chain-specific schema (embedded and external DefraDB) via `GetSchemaForChain`.
  - Pass the chain-specific collections into `BlockHandler` and pruner queue tracking.
  - Log the active chain and prefix at startup.
- Update unit and integration tests to work with the new constructor signatures and dynamic collection naming.

## Related Issue
Resolves #130 

## Steps to Test
1. Pull branch locally.
2. Build and run tests:
   - `go test ./...`
3. Run the indexer with default config (Ethereum Mainnet):
   - Confirm collections/types are created as `Ethereum__Mainnet__*` and indexing still works.
4. Run the indexer with a non-default chain, e.g.:
   - Set `CHAIN_NAME=Arbitrum`, `CHAIN_NETWORK=Mainnet` (or update `config.yaml` accordingly).
   - Start the indexer and ensure:
     - Schema types/collections are created as `Arbitrum__Mainnet__Block`, `Arbitrum__Mainnet__Transaction`, etc.
     - Blocks, transactions, logs, and access list entries are written to those collections.
     - Pruner still operates correctly on the new collection names.
5. Optionally verify external DefraDB mode:
   - Point `DEFRADB_URL` to an external DefraDB instance.
   - Ensure schema application succeeds and indexing works with the configured chain prefix.

## Checklist
- [x] Code compiles / runs
- [x] Tests added / updated
- [ ] Documentation updated if needed
- [x] PR is self-contained and focused
- [x] Code does not break any existing features
- [x] Code passes personal internal testing


## Notes
- The naming convention used is `{chainName}__{network}__Type` (e.g. `Arbitrum__Mainnet__Block`) rather than a numeric `chainID__EVM__Type`; if the project wants the literal `chainID__EVM` pattern, we can adjust `chainPrefixFromConfig` / `ChainConfig` in a follow-up.

author: copilot
body:
Adds two focused and independent CMake helper modules for on-target embedded testing via SEGGER J-Run and CTest, following the same style as `meta_gtest.cmake`.

- `tools/cmake/meta_unity.cmake` — Unity test executable builder (mirrors `meta_gtest`): creates or extends an `add_executable` target for the firmware test binary, appends `SOURCES` incrementally, and links `LINK` libraries. The caller's CMake toolchain file controls the cross-compiler. No J-Run or CTest involvement.
- `tools/cmake/meta_jrun.cmake` — generic J-Run CTest runner: validates the firmware `TARGET` as an existing `EXECUTABLE`, finds `JRun` (idempotent via `meta_jrun_exe` cache variable), applies defaults for `INTERFACE`/`SPEED`/`TIMEOUT`, and registers CTest tests. When `SUITES` are provided, registers one namespaced `<TARGET>.<suite>` CTest test per suite, forwarding the suite name to the firmware via J-Run `--args`. When no `SUITES` are specified, registers a single CTest test for the entire binary.
- The two modules are completely independent and are composed by the caller in `CMakeLists.txt`.
- CTest test names are namespaced as `<TARGET>.<suite>` to avoid collisions across targets.
- `TARGET` is validated as an existing CMake `EXECUTABLE` at configure time with actionable `FATAL_ERROR` messages in `meta_jrun`.
- `INTERFACE` is validated against the allowed set (`SWD`, `JTAG`) at configure time with an actionable `FATAL_ERROR` message in `meta_jrun`.
- `tools/cmake/README.md` documents all CMake helper modules including `meta_jrun` (section 1.5) and `meta_unity` (section 1.8) with prerequisites, usage signatures, and a combined usage example.

Cardholders often juggle multiple credit cards with expiring 0% APR promotional rates. Without proper tracking, they risk missing transfer windows and incurring high interest rates (18-25%) when promos end.

`progress_bar` used `**kwargs: dict` which incorrectly types each kwarg value as `dict` — a problem exposed to consumers via the `py.typed` marker. The four optional display parameters are now explicit with proper `str` types.

## Changes

- **`progress_bar` signature**: replaced `**kwargs: dict` with `prefix: str = ""`, `suffix: str = ""`, `fill: str = "█"`, `print_end: str = "\r"`
- Removed the `kwargs.get()` extraction block; values are now direct parameters
- Updated docstring to document each parameter individually
- Added `# pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments` — same pattern already used in `scanner.py`

```python
# Before
def progress_bar(iterable, decimals=1, length=50, **kwargs: dict) -> Collection:
    prefix = kwargs.get('prefix', '')  # typed as dict, not str

# After
def progress_bar(
    iterable: Collection,
    decimals: int = 1,
    length: int = 50,
    prefix: str = "",
    suffix: str = "",
    fill: str = "█",
    print_end: str = "\r",
) -> Collection:
```

author: darkgnotic
body:
Fixes ddl event logic to detect when a table is removed from the published schema, e.g.

```sql
ALTER TABLE foo SET SCHEMA not_published;
```

The previous logic incorrectly ignored such events because the table was not part of the publication; it did not account for the possibility that the table was previously part of the publication (i.e. prior to the ddl command). 

The fix is to handle ALTER TABLE statements in the same manner as DROP statements, i.e. by generating ddl updates and letting the zero-cache filter based on the diff.

### Motivation
- Ensure stable upserts by detecting and removing duplicate student rows in Google Sheets when multiple rows match the same StudentCode/UID/Email.
- Avoid incorrect column mapping caused by duplicate or stray headers farther to the right of the sheet by preferring the first occurrence of a normalized header.
- Provide safer sheet tab handling and batch row deletions to support robust server-side sync operations.

### Description
- Add `getTabSheetId` and `deleteDuplicateRows` helpers to look up a sheet tab's numeric `sheetId` and perform batch row deletions via `spreadsheets.batchUpdate`.
- Change header mapping in both `api/sync-student.js` and `functions/functionz/studentsSheet.js` to keep the first normalized header occurrence so right-side duplicate headers do not override canonical columns (`headerIndex`/`headerMap` dedupe).
- Replace single-match lookup with a collected-match approach (`collectMatchingRows`) to find all rows matching `StudentCode`, `UID`, or `Email`, pick the first as the canonical row, and remove any additional duplicate rows.
- Update upsert logic to compute `rowNumber`/`sheetRowNumber` from the sorted set of matches and to perform safe per-cell updates only for existing columns.
- Preserve backwards-compatible header alias resolution for columns like `StudentCode`, `UID`, `Email`, `Name`, `Paid`, `Balance`, and others.

Replace the custom `LayoutField` with a `LayoutSerializer` using DRF's built-in `IntegerField` validators to reject invalid widget dimensions at the API level.

Widgets created via external tools (e.g. LLMs) can have invalid dimensions like `w: 12` where the grid maximum is `6`. This change prevents such layouts from being persisted. The `LayoutSerializer` also lets drf-spectacular auto-generate accurate OpenAPI documentation with field types and constraints, removing the need for manual `@extend_schema_field` annotations.

# 🔐 Implement AES-256-GCM Encryption + Structured Audit Logging

Closes #83  
Closes #81  

---

## 📌 Summary

This PR implements secure **AES-256-GCM encryption** for custodial wallet secret keys and introduces **structured audit logging** for sensitive wallet operations.

It replaces insecure encryption logic, adds authenticated encryption with upgrade support, and ensures all critical wallet actions are traceable with redacted structured logs.

---

## 🚀 Changes

### 1️⃣ AES-256-GCM Encryption  
**File:** `backend/src/utils/encryption.ts`

- Implemented envelope encryption format:
  - `version`
  - `algo`
  - `iv`
  - `ciphertext`
  - `tag`
- Added:
  - `encrypt()` — AES-256-GCM encryption
  - `decrypt()` — Authenticated decryption with tag verification
  - `generateMasterKey()` — Secure 32-byte key generation
  - `getActiveMasterKey()` — Environment-based key selection (v1/v2 support)
- Ensures:
  - Unique IV per encryption
  - Authentication tag validation
  - Future upgrade path via versioning

---

### 2️⃣ Wallet Service Integration  
**File:** `backend/src/services/custodialWalletService.ts`

- Replaced insecure XOR encryption with AES-256-GCM
- Added `AesGcmDecryptor` class
- Updated `EncryptedKeyRecord` interface to support envelope structure
- Ensures all stored wallet secrets use authenticated encryption

---

### 3️⃣ Structured Audit Logging  
**File:** `backend/src/utils/auditLogger.ts`

Introduced structured JSON logging format with:

- `eventType`
- `userId`
- `requestId`
- `ip`
- `actorType`
- `timestamp`
- `metadata`

Automatic secret redaction:
- passwords

- tokens

### 4️⃣ Route Instrumentation

### 5️⃣ Environment Configuration

Documented:
- `CUSTODIAL_WALLET_MASTER_KEY_V1`

Includes instructions for secure key generation.

---

### Motivation
- Prevent the cue ball from remaining lost/off-table after a pocket/scratch and make ball-in-hand placement feel smoother and safer. 
- Make the cue-stick visual/perspective feedback clearer by showing a larger lift and a visible pull/push motion that doesn't snap back unexpectedly. 
- Ensure camera height/rail/cushion calculations remain correct when table/ball/rail assets are adjusted.

### Description
- Added configurable fields to `CueCamera` for asset height offsets and cue-stick visuals: `cueStickExtraLift`, `tableAssetHeightOffset`, `cueStickMaxPull`, `cueStickMaxPush`, and `cueStickStrokeSmooth` so pull/push and camera lift are tunable. 
- Implemented smooth cue-stick stroke input via `SetCueStickStroke(float)` and applied exponential smoothing to the visual stroke and cue distance so the stick shows pull and push without snapping. 
- Implemented auto-recovery for a pocketed/deactivated cue ball with `TrackCueBallScratchAndRestore()` and `RestoreCueBallForBallInHand()` which re-enables the cue ball, clamps it inside rails using `ClampCueBallToTable()`, resets rigidbody motion, and activates ball-in-hand. 
- Added smooth ball-in-hand repositioning: serialized parameters `ballInHandMoveLerpSpeed`, `ballInHandRailInset`, `cueBallResetHeightOffset`, public API `SetBallInHandPosition(Vector3)`, and per-frame movement via `MoveCueBallTowardTarget(float)` to lerp the cue ball toward the placement target. 
- Updated camera math to respect `tableAssetHeightOffset` for rail clearance and pocket-drop checks, and added `cueStickExtraLift` to raise the aiming view so the shaft clears updated rails.

### Testing
- Performed a code review and repository consistency checks on the modified file `billiards.Unity/CueCamera.cs`; no edit conflicts or whitespace issues were reported. 
- No automated unit or playmode tests were executed as part of this patch; recommended next steps are running the Unity Editor playmode tests and manual in-editor smoke checks (scratch/cue-in-hand flows and cue stroke visuals) to validate runtime behavior on the target builds.

author: triltsch
body:
## Issue #26: Sprint 2 [S2-BE-05] Upload Retry + Timeout Handling

Fixes #26

### Summary
Implemented comprehensive timeout guardrails and retry semantics for the upload API, ensuring robust handling of transient failures and explicit visibility into upload operation states.

### Changes Implemented

#### 1. Timeout Enforcement (10 minutes)
- Set `UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` in `app/config.py`
- Enforced timeout for file read and MinIO upload operations via `asyncio.wait_for()`
- Added `TimeoutError` handling that converts to `StorageError` for consistent error propagation

#### 2. Transient Retry Semantics
- Added `_is_transient_error()` classification method in storage adapter
  - Classifies errors as transient (should retry) or terminal (fail fast)
  - Transient indicators: timeout, connection, 503, 429, DNS, network resets
- Added `_retry_backoff_seconds()` exponential backoff with bounded maximum
  - Formula: `min(2.0, 0.25 * (2**attempt))` caps backoff at 2 seconds
  - Sequence: 0.25s → 0.5s → 1.0s → 2.0s (for attempts 0-3+)
  - With 3 retries: total delay ≤ 6 seconds (well within 600-second timeout)
- Non-transient errors fail fast without retry loop

#### 3. Failure State Visibility in API Response
- Extended `UploadErrorResponse` with explicit retry policy fields:
  - `failure_state`: Current operation state (value: "failed")
  - `retryable`: Boolean indicating if retry is recommended
  - `retry_after_seconds`: Suggested wait time before retry
- Router returns HTTP 503 (Service Unavailable) with structured error payload
- Added `Retry-After: 30` HTTP header following RFC 7231 standard
- Enables client-side retry policies based on structured error information

#### 4. HTTP Client Timeout Configuration
- Configured urllib3 `Timeout` in MinIO storage adapter
  - `total=600`: Overall operation timeout
  - `connect=10`: Connection establishment timeout
  - `read=600`: Response read timeout
- Disables urllib3 automatic retries in favor of custom retry logic

### Files Modified
- `app/config.py`: Added `UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600`
- `app/modules/upload/storage.py`: Transient error classification, exponential backoff, timeout config
- `app/modules/upload/service.py`: Async timeout enforcement via `asyncio.wait_for()`
- `app/modules/upload/router.py`: Structured 503 error response with retry policy
- `app/modules/upload/schemas.py`: Extended `UploadErrorResponse` with retry fields
- `tests/modules/upload/test_service.py`: Added timeout enforcement test
- `tests/modules/upload/test_storage.py`: Added non-transient error no-retry test
- `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`: Issue #26 completion documentation
- `LEARNINGS.md`: Async timeout patterns and retry semantics learnings

### Acceptance Criteria - All Met
- ✅ **Timeout limit set to 10 minutes for upload operation**
  - Evidence: `UPLOAD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` enforced via `asyncio.wait_for()`
  
- ✅ **Retry path available for transient failures**
  - Evidence: `_is_transient_error()` + `_retry_backoff_seconds()` + 3-attempt retry logic
  
- ✅ **Failure state is visible in API response contract**
  - Evidence: `UploadErrorResponse` includes `failure_state`, `retryable`, `retry_after_seconds`

### Test Results
- **240/240 tests passing** ✅
- **89% code coverage** ✅ (exceeds 70% requirement)
- **New tests**: 
  - `test_create_nano_upload_timeout_raises_storage_error()` - Validates timeout enforcement
  - `test_upload_file_non_transient_failure_no_retry()` - Validates fast-fail for terminal errors
- **Updated tests**: Storage error integration test assertions updated for structured response

### Docker Environment Validation
- ✅ All Docker services healthy (postgres, redis, minio, meilisearch, app)
- ✅ Redis connectivity verified
- ✅ MinIO bucket instantiation successful
- ✅ Configuration alignment verified across docker-compose.yml, .env.example, app/config.py

### Key Technical Decisions

**Exponential Backoff with Bounded Maximum**
- Prevents unbounded growth from exceeding timeout window
- 2-second maximum backoff allows quick recovery from transient failures
- 3 retry attempts with ≤6 seconds total delay (well within 600-second timeout)

**Transient Classification via Pattern Matching**
- Works across library exception hierarchies (MinIO SDK errors)
- Maintainable: add transient indicators as new failure modes discovered
- Avoids broad exception catching that hides bugs

**Structured Error Response Contract**
- Follows REST best practices (HTTP 503 + Retry-After header)
- Enables client-side retry policies without response parsing hacks
- Explicit `retryable` field prevents retry loop anti-patterns

**Async Timeout with Thread Pool Integration**
- `asyncio.wait_for()` for hard deadline enforcement
- `asyncio.to_thread()` for synchronous MinIO SDK without blocking event loop
- Clean async/await semantics while handling blocking I/O

### Documentation Added
- Comprehensive learnings in `LEARNINGS.md` covering:
  - Async timeout enforcement patterns
  - Transient error classification strategies
  - Exponential backoff formula derivation
  - Structured error responses for client retry policies
  - Thread pool integration with async/await
  - HTTP client timeout configuration

---

**Note**: This PR implements the complete S2-BE-05 feature from the Sprint 2 roadmap (story 2.1). All acceptance criteria met, all tests passing, Docker environment validated.

LayerGradientXActivation is having a number of jobs with OOM erros. These errors are due to the way we drain GPU memory during the forward and backward passes to obtain layer evaluations, copies of evaluations, and layer gradients.

The issue with the current way of getting evalutaions and gradients is the following:

* After getting the evaluations (activations) from the forward pass, we gather all the activation tensors across multiple devices into [one device](https://www.internalfb.com/code/fbsource/[0579e5aab76b1f89fc82d27913cbb3a6e0160b5f]/fbcode/pytorch/captum/captum/_utils/common.py?lines=785) meaning that one device would hold its own layer activations + copy of all the activations across all devices. This is the peak of the memory utilization. This is in addition to storing the model graph and the original layer activations in memory.


* After the backward pass on the `saved_layer` (still on GPU), we are also doing a similar operation on the gradients - collecting gradients across all devices into the first device. At this point though, we don't have as much memory utilization since backward pass is already completed. So it is safer to collect all gradients. We can then offload to cpu afterwards.

What we want to do now is to offload the layer activations to cpu during these peak gpu utilization. Before we run the expensive torch.cat, we offload all these tensors to cpu first. That way, when we run torch.cat, this is actually done on cpu freeing up gpu memory.

Additionally when we get to the gradients, after gathering all tensors together, we also offload these to cpu.

With this simple change, we would significantly improve gpu utilization. We add a flag that will include an efficient path to the implementation.

Adds a `memory_efficient` mode to `LayerGradientXActivation` and an `offload_to_cpu` parameter to `compute_layer_gradients_and_eval` to reduce peak GPU memory usage during multi-layer attribution.

author: refcell
body:
## Summary

Changes `BlobData::fill` to return `Result<bool, BlobProviderError>` instead of `Result<bool, BlobDecodingError>`, so that blob under-fill is treated as a recoverable reset condition rather than a permanent critical failure. Previously,
when a blob provider returned fewer blobs than expected, the pipeline would halt indefinitely. Now it resets and retries from the last safe L1 block, matching the behavior of the Go op-node which wraps the same condition as
`NewResetError` in `fillBlobPointers`.

A new `ResetError::BlobsUnderFill(usize, usize)` variant is added to the pipeline error hierarchy, and
`BlobProviderError::NotEnoughBlobs(usize, usize)` is added as the surface-level error that maps to it. The `B256`
import in `base-consensus-genesis` is tightened to its `#[cfg(feature = "serde")]` use site, and missing `std` feature
propagation entries are added to `base-proof-driver`, `base-proof-executor`, and `base-proof-mpt` per zepter.

Closes #996. Upstream: ethereum-optimism/optimism#19362.

body:
## Summary

Replace `apca-w3` and `culori` dependencies with clean-room implementations derived from public specifications. This resolves license compliance issues with both libraries.

## Changes

### New engine modules
- **`src/engine/ApcaEngine.ts`** — APCA 0.98G-4g algorithm from [W3C Silver Wiki spec](https://www.w3.org/WAI/GL/task-forces/silver/wiki/User:Myndex/APCA_model). Implements sRGBtoY, soft-clamp, and polarity-aware Lc formula with documented constants.
- **`src/engine/OklchMathEngine.ts`** — sRGB ↔ Linear RGB ↔ OKLab ↔ OKLCH pipeline from [Björn Ottosson's OKLab paper](https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/) + CSS Color Level 4. Includes gamut checking, binary-search chroma clamping, and color string parsing.

### Integration
- SDK `contrast.ts`: removed lazy-loading pattern, uses built-in ApcaEngine
- CLI `apca.ts` + `lint.ts`: replaced apca-w3 imports with ApcaEngine
- `OklchEngine.ts`: replaced all culori/fn imports with OklchMathEngine
- Removed `registerApca()` / `isApcaAvailable()` — APCA is now always available

### Default mode change
- SDK contrast default changed from `wcag` to `apca`, aligning with CLI
- WCAG 2.x still available via `.mode('wcag')`

### Dependency cleanup
- Removed `apca-w3` from SDK (peer + dev), CLI, and root
- Removed `culori` from SDK, CLI, and root
- Deleted `sdk/src/apca-w3.d.ts`
- Removed `--external apca-w3` from SDK build script

## Performance

Benchmarked against original libraries (2M APCA evals, 1M OKLCH ops):

| Operation | Ours | Original | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| APCA contrast | 350ms | 526ms | **1.50× faster** |
| Hex → OKLCH | 118ms | 149ms | **1.26× faster** |
| OKLCH → Hex | 159ms | 120ms | 0.75× |
| Gamut check | 64ms | 71ms | **1.11× faster** |

## Parity

- **APCA**: 0.0000 Lc difference across all 20 test pairs (bit-identical)
- **OKLCH**: All hex roundtrips identical, L/C values match to machine epsilon (~2e-16)

## Tests

- ✅ 137 SDK tests pass
- ✅ 202 CLI tests pass
- ✅ TypeScript type check passes
- ✅ SDK builds successfully

`bed_spam_click_delay` was defined in config but not consistently used in AH grace-period click loops. This updates the click interval wiring so configurable bed spam uses config, while keeping the existing freemoney bed-timing cadence unchanged.

- **Config wiring**
  - Plumbed `config.bed_spam_click_delay` into runtime state (`BotClient` → `BotClientState`) so AH handlers can consume it directly.

- **Grace-period spam now respects config**
  - Replaced hardcoded interval in the chat-triggered grace-period spam loop with `state.bed_spam_click_delay` (clamped to `>= 1ms`).

- **Bed timing behavior intentionally preserved**
  - Kept the freemoney timing path on fixed `100ms` cadence.
  - Applied config interval only to non-freemoney bed spam path.

- **Config parsing coverage**
  - Added a focused config test ensuring `bed_spam_click_delay` is parsed from TOML.

```rust
let click_interval_ms = if state.freemoney {
    100 // keep existing bed timing cadence
} else {
    state.bed_spam_click_delay.max(1) // config-driven spam interval
};
```

author: fredm-spotify
body:
This attempts to fix an issue when Kapt generates Java code that requires access to internal classes that are stripped from ABI jars. @rbeazleyspot has opened an issue https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_kotlin/issues/1467 with much more detail and another approach at fixing it. This is a simpler way to go about it and we wanted your advice on these.

When `experimental_remove_private_classes_in_abi_jars` is enabled `associate[JavaInfo].compile_jars` doesn't contain internal symbols. However, Kapt might generate code that requires access to these. An example is the Dagger generated code. 

If a target `B` associates with a target `A` and `B` is generating Dagger code, the call to `java_common.compile` in `_run_kt_java_builder_actions` doesn't seem to have access to the internal symbols from the associates array. Hence, compilation of the Java code fails.

author: cdvelop
body:
Adds a `FormatISO8601` function to the `tinywasm/time` package.

Context:
The `tinywasm/time` package previously formatted strings with local time offsets unconditionally. To support systems like FHIR which require raw UTC timestamps in the standard `RFC3339`/`ISO8601` format (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`), this dedicated formatter ignores the offset and returns strict UTC.

Implementation details:
- Standard Go (`!wasm`): Uses `time.Unix(0, nano).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339)`
- WebAssembly (`wasm`): Uses JavaScript's native Date `.toISOString()` output, strictly truncated and suffixed to exactly match `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

Also includes a fix to the WASM timer testing and updates the README.

## Description
Adds automated testing of Python code examples in the documentation to prevent examples from drifting out of sync with the library.

- Add `mktestdocs` and `pytest` to the `doc` dependency group in `pyproject.toml` so they are available alongside the other doc-build tools without pulling in the full `dev` group.

- Add `tests/check-docs-drift.py`: a pytest-based script that uses `mktestdocs.grab_code_blocks()` to collect every ```python fenced block under `docs/`, skips any block whose first line is `# skip`, and executes the rest via `exec_python()`. A new taskipy task `docs-check-drift` runs it with `pytest scripts/check-docs-drift.py -v`.

- Fix all ```python code blocks across `docs/` so they are correctly picked up by mktestdocs. Some are marked "#skip" because it's infeasible to run them in CI.

- Set `save_to_file=False, log_level="error"` via environment variables in check-docs-drift.py to avoid creating CSV files or noisy output during CI runs.
 
- Update `.github/workflows/build-docs.yml` to run `docs-check-drift` as a step before the docs build, triggered on changes to `docs/**`, `mkdocs.yml`, or `scripts/check-docs-drift.py`.

- Document the drift check and the `# skip` convention in `CONTRIBUTING.md` under the "Build Documentation" section.

author: skialpine
body:
Fixes #341 — Bookoo scale tare oscillation causing SAW failures.

## Root Causes

1. **Drip cap missing**: First-shot `getExpectedDrip()` used `flow × 1.5` with no cap. At flow=12 g/s this predicted 18g drip on a 36g target, firing SAW immediately.

2. **One-way oscillation latch**: Detecting oscillation (`weight < -5g`) set `m_tareComplete = false` permanently — `setTareComplete()` is only called once per shot, so SAW stayed disabled for the entire shot.

3. **Sparse scale LSLR underflow**: Bookoo reports at ~2Hz. The 500ms short window contained only 1–2 samples, making LSLR return 0 and gating out SAW.

4. **Generic sensor lag**: First-shot used a universal 1.5s lag rather than per-scale empirical values from de1app.

## Changes

### Stop-at-Weight
- Cap first-shot drip default at 8g on all fallback paths (`flow × lag + 8g` cap)
- Add mid-shot oscillation recovery: 3 consecutive near-zero readings re-arm SAW with a fresh LSLR baseline, mirroring de1app's `_tare_awaiting_zero / on_tare_seen` pattern
- `setTareComplete(true)` now also clears oscillation state — fixes stuck `m_oscillationDetected` if scale reconnects or source switches mid-shot
- Adaptive short LSLR window: `shortWindowMs = max(500, span_of_last_3 + 50, capped at 1000ms)` — ensures 2–3 samples at 2Hz vs. 1–2 at fixed 500ms
- Post-shot interval logging in `stopExtraction()` to confirm scale reporting rate in shot debug log

### SAW Learning
- Per-scale sensor lag table from de1app (Acaia 0.69s, Bookoo/Felicita 0.50s, Hiroia 0.25s, Decent/Skale 0.38s) for first-shot defaults
- Added Acaia Pyxis (0.69s) which was missing from the lookup
- `qWarning` for unknown scale types in `sensorLag()` to surface gaps in shot debug log
- Implied-lag plausibility guard: reject learning entries where `drip/flow > 4s`
- Outlier rejection skipped when auto-reset is due (`overshoot < -6g`)
- Auto-reset SAW history after 2 consecutive early stops (>6g under target)

### Tare Timeout
- 3s → 6s fallback timeout for hot-water tare (Bookoo takes up to 5s to settle post-tare)

### Code Quality
- Convert static throttle log vars to member vars reset in `startExtraction()` — prevents warning suppression across consecutive shots
- `getExpectedDrip()` reads `scaleType()` once at top for consistency across all fallback paths
- Guard zero span in `stopExtraction()` Hz calculation to avoid `inf` in shot debug log
- Pre-compute `sensorLagSeconds` before inner lambda in `main.cpp` (fix uncaptured variable UB in `QueuedConnection`)

## Testing
Verified against de1app Tcl source (`device_scale.tcl`):
- BLE UUIDs and commands identical
- Scale-specific sensor lag values match de1app's empirical table
- Oscillation recovery pattern mirrors de1app's `_tare_awaiting_zero` mechanism

author: copilot
body:
GlitchGetaway lacked persistent identity and competitive replay value — anonymous sessions, no score tracking, no reason to replay.

## New model: `GameSession`
Tracks a single play-through linked to an optional authenticated user. Uses `default=timezone.now` (not `auto_now_add`) so start time can be set explicitly in tests.

```python
class GameSession(models.Model):
    user = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL)
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=50, default='Anonymous')
    started_at = models.DateTimeField(default=timezone.now)
    finished_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    total_attempts = models.PositiveIntegerField(default=0)
    completed = models.BooleanField(default=False)
```

## User accounts
- Register / login / logout via Django's built-in auth — no third-party packages
- Anonymous play fully supported; username shown in game header when authenticated

## Live game timer
- `home` creates a `GameSession` and stores its ID in the session
- `room.html` receives the ISO start timestamp; JS ticks `[[ TIMER ]] MM:SS` every second
- Wrong attempts incremented in the DB on each bad guess and displayed live alongside the timer

## Leaderboard (`/play/leaderboard/`)
- Top-10 completions ordered by elapsed time then wrong guesses via **database-level annotation** — no Python-side sorting
- `leaderboard` accepted as a terminal command mid-game

```python
def _leaderboard_qs():
    return (
        GameSession.objects.filter(completed=True)
        .annotate(elapsed=ExpressionWrapper(
            F('finished_at') - F('started_at'), output_field=DurationField()
        ))
        .order_by('elapsed', 'total_attempts')
    )
```

author: vpulim
body:
## Summary
Fixes breaking changes introduced by upgrading `marked` from v11 to v17 and `@mariozechner/pi-agent-core` from 0.52 to 0.55. These are major version bumps that changed fundamental APIs.

## Key Changes

**marked v17 renderer migration** (`src/cli/utils/markdown.ts`)
- Updated all renderer methods to use token objects instead of positional arguments
- Added `this` context binding to access `this.parser.parseInline(tokens)` for inline content and `this.parser.parse(tokens)` for block content
- Fixed `list()` renderer: cannot pass `token.items` directly to parser (parser doesn't recognize `list_item` tokens). Now manually iterates items and calls `this.listitem(item)` for each
- Updated method signatures for: `heading`, `paragraph`, `strong`, `em`, `codespan`, `code`, `list`, `listitem`, `link`, and `blockquote`

**pi-agent-core AuthStorage migration** (`src/agent/runners/pi-session.ts`)
- Changed `new AuthStorage(path)` to `AuthStorage.create(path)` — constructor is now private and factory methods are required

## Implementation Details

The marked v17 migration required understanding that the renderer's `list()` method receives a token object with an `items` array, but the parser's `parse()` method doesn't recognize `list_item` tokens directly. The solution is to iterate the items manually and delegate to `this.listitem()` for each item, which then calls `this.parser.parse(item.tokens)` to render the item's content.

All renderer methods now properly type-check against the `Tokens` type from marked, ensuring type safety across the migration.

body:
When `--local-addr` is configured with a mix of IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (e.g. `--local-addr 192.168.1.1,2001:db8::1`), SetRandomLocalAddr picks one at random without considering the target's address family. This causes scans to fail intermittently. Whenever the randomly chosen local address doesn't match the target's protocol (e.g. binding an IPv6 source for an IPv4 destination), the OS rejects the connection and your grab attempt fails with `{"ip":"2607:f8b0:400a:809::200e","data":{"http":{"status":"connection-timeout","protocol":"http","port":80,"result":{},"timestamp":"2026-02-27T13:38:26-08:00","error":"unable to dial target (2607:f8b0:400a:809::200e) with L4 Dialer: dial context failed: dial tcp: address 10.10.9.92:0: no suitable address found"}}}`

## How to Test

Run this command a few times with the existing implementation:
```
echo 2607:f8b0:400a:809::200e | ./zgrab2 http --local-addr=[your ipv4 here],[your ipv6 here]
```
It will fail 50% of the time. Then test mine and confirm that it works consistently.

## Notes & Caveats

I've tested this patch locally and it works. However I'm not a particularly experienced Go dev and this is my first time looking at the zgrab2 source code, so feedback is welcome and appreciated. In particular, I'm not sure if `filterLocalAddrsByFamily`'s current return behavior is reasonable or if I should be returning an error.

This change serves to split the Pokédex Area's encounter data into Day time and Night time.

When the user opens the Area screen, it prepares the encounter data for the current game's time (night/day) for display. During that it also caches the alternative time's data and areaGlowTilemap. While the fade out/in happens it also tints the palette for the map if the user's game is during night time - this serves as a visual indicator for the user for which mode they are currently in. Once the area screen is loaded, the user can hit the START button to flip between Night time encounters and Day time encounters. For the day time map, I added an access point for the screen to read the map's normal palette directly from ROM - no caching necessary.

The new day/night indicators in the bottom left share the AREA UNKNOWN's palette tag, so that they play nicely with the fade-in/out when going to/leaving the area screen.

author: kylecarbs
body:
## Problem

The subscribe flow in `useWebpushNotifications` called `pushManager.subscribe()` without first requesting the `Notification` permission. When the browser permission state is `"denied"` (e.g. from a previous prompt dismissal), the browser throws:

```
DOMException: Registration failed - permission denied
```

This surfaced as a confusing error toast on the agents page. The error has nothing to do with Coder RBAC roles — it's the browser denying the push subscription because notification permission was previously declined. An admin who had granted browser permission wouldn't see this; a user who previously dismissed or denied the prompt would.

## Fix

Added an explicit `Notification.requestPermission()` call before `pushManager.subscribe()`. This:

1. **Re-prompts** the user if the permission state is `"default"` (not yet decided)
2. **Throws a clear, actionable error** if the permission is `"denied"`: *"Notifications are blocked by your browser. Please allow notifications for this site in your browser settings."*
3. **Only proceeds** to `pushManager.subscribe()` after permission is confirmed as `"granted"`

## Tests

New test file `useWebpushNotifications.jest.ts`:
- **requests notification permission before subscribing** — verifies `requestPermission()` is called before `pushManager.subscribe()`
- **throws a clear error when permission is denied** — verifies the user-friendly error message
- **does not call pushManager.subscribe when permission is denied** — verifies we bail out early

author: kaisercgn-lab
body:
💡 **What:**
Wrapped the `positionedEvents` array mapping inside a `useMemo` hook, using `[events]` as its dependency array.

🎯 **Why:**
The `positionedEvents` array creation mapped over the `events` prop on *every single render* of the `TimelineHero` component, allocating a new array and new objects. These newly allocated objects caused unnecessary memory overhead and garbage collection cycles during state changes (such as dragging the timeline or toggling the `isExpanded` state). By memoizing the array, the component only recalculates the mapped objects when the `events` prop changes.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
Since this React component lacks existing tests or benchmarking infrastructure (e.g., benchmark.js setup), I was unable to establish an empirical benchmark measuring the specific cost of the unmemoized array. However, this optimization is a targeted structural improvement to avoid unnecessary instantiation and garbage collection. Preventing new array and object creations on every render reduces main thread blocking during user interactions, resulting in smoother scroll/drag performance over time.

author: devjakov
body:
Previously the dashboard calculated email-attributed % as:
  totalEmailRevenue / businessRevenue
which produced impossible results like 99.1% when email revenue ≈ business revenue.

The correct model:
- ~20% of Klaviyo-reported email revenue would have occurred without email (last-touch attribution bias, most common in welcome flows)
- incrementalEmailRevenue = totalEmailRevenue × 80%
- trueNewTotalRevenue = businessRevenue + incrementalEmailRevenue (e.g. $400k base + $320k incremental = $720k, not $800k)
- emailAttributedPercent = incrementalEmailRevenue / trueNewTotalRevenue (e.g. $320k / $720k = 44.4%, not 99.1%)

Changes:
- Added LAST_TOUCH_OVERLAP_RATE = 0.20 constant with detailed explanation
- Calculations useMemo: adds incrementalEmailRevenue, lastTouchRevenue, trueNewTotalRevenue, emailAttributedPercent; removes emailPercentOfRevenue
- Scenario calculations: same 80% correction applied to emailPercent
- Dashboard: "Total Email Revenue" card replaced with "Total Monthly Revenue" showing a stacked bar — base revenue (translucent white) + email-incremental revenue (green-to-emerald gradient) with correct % label
- Footer: added * footnote explaining the last-touch attribution adjustment

author: davidhewitt
body:
This WIP attempts to pass vm around more places instead of `heap, interns` as separate pieces borrowed out of VM. This _might_ help me with problems I'm facing in #207, but it's possible there are other ways to solve it.

I think this refactoring would be necessary if monty ever supports the `class` statement, as the vm would be needed to run all the user code for magic methods such as `__len__` etc.

I think it might also be completely reasonably to not do this and commit to not supporting user-defined classes. I can imagine that user-defined classes are extremely hard to support in the face of suspendable execution, as basically the entire interpreter could suspend at any point, so I think a lot of the code which is currently implemented as Rust would instead have to be rewritten as micro-ops which could be individually suspended. (That might ultimately pay out, but it seems risky / hard / potentially impossible for all code paths, such as when finding hash entry inside a dictionary.)
